साधुबुद्ध्यास दुष्टात्मा किं चकार महामते ॥
2.30.m: to whom I offered hospitality duly according to rule / with pious intent? What did that wicked soul do, O high-minded one?”

2.30.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
evaṃ sa pṛṣṭo matimānbhṛguḥ sarvavidīśvaraḥ /
ciraṃ dhyātvā samālocya kāraṇaṃ prāha bhūpate //
2.30.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
एवं स पृष्टो मतिमान्भृगुः सर्वविदीश्वरः ।
चिरं ध्यात्वा समालोच्य कारणं प्राह भूपते ॥
2.30.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
Thus questioned, the wise Bhṛgu, the all-knowing lord, / having meditated long and reflected upon the cause, spoke, O king.

2.30.s:
bhṛguruvāca
śṛṇu tāta mahābhāga bījamasya hi karmaṇaḥ /
yaśca vai kṛtavānpāpaṃ sarvajñasya tavānagha //
2.30.d:
भृगुरुवाच
शृणु तात महाभाग बीजमस्य हि कर्मणः ।
यश्च वै कृतवान्पापं सर्वज्ञस्य तवानघ ॥
2.30.m:
Bhṛgu said:
“Listen, my dear fortunate one, to the seed of this deed / and of the sin which he committed against you who are all-knowing and sinless.

2.30.s:
śaptaḥ purā vasiṣṭhena nāśārthaṃ sa mahīpatiḥ /
dvijāparādhato mūḍha vīryaṃ te vinaśiṣyate //
2.30.d:
शप्तः पुरा वसिष्ठेन नाशार्थं स महीपतिः ।
द्विजापराधतो मूढ वीर्यं ते विनशिष्यते ॥
2.30.m:
Formerly that lord of the earth was cursed by Vasiṣṭha for his destruction:
‘Because of an offense against a twice-born, O fool, your valor shall perish!’

2.30.s:
tatkathaṃ vacanaṃ tasya bhaviṣyatyanyathā muneḥ /
ayaṃ rāmo mahāvīryaṃ prasahyanṛpapuṅgavam //
2.30.d:
तत्कथं वचनं तस्य भविष्यत्यन्यथा मुनेः ।
अयं रामो महावीर्यं प्रसह्यनृपपुङ्गवम् ॥
2.30.m: How then will that word of the sage turn out otherwise? / This Rāma, overpowering the bull of kings possessed of great valor,

2.30.s:
haniṣyati mahābāho pratijñāṃ kṛtavānpurā /
yasmāduraḥ pratihataṃ tvayā mātarmamāgrataḥ //
2.30.d:
हनिष्यति महाबाहो प्रतिज्ञां कृतवान्पुरा ।
यस्मादुरः प्रतिहतं त्वया मातर्ममाग्रतः ॥
2.30.m:
shall slay him, O mighty-armed one! Formerly he made a vow:
‘Because, O mother, your breast was struck before me

2.30.s:
ekaviṃśativāraṃ hi bhṛśaṃ duḥkhaparītayā /
triḥ saptakṛtvo niḥkṣatrāṃ kariṣye pṛthivīmimām //
2.30.d:
एकविंशतिवारं हि भृशं दुःखपरीतया ।
त्रिः सप्तकृत्वो निःक्षत्रां करिष्ये पृथिवीमिमाम् ॥
2.30.m: twenty-one times by you who were overwhelmed with intense grief, / thrice seven times I will make this earth bereft of kṣatriyas!’

2.30.s:
ato 'yaṃ vāryamāṇo 'pi tvāyā pitrā nirantaram /
bhāvinor'thasya ca balātkariṣyatyeva mānada //
2.30.d:
अतो ऽयं वार्यमाणो ऽपि त्वाया पित्रा निरन्तरम् ।
भाविनोर्ऽथस्य च बलात्करिष्यत्येव मानद ॥
2.30.m: Therefore, even though continuously restrained by you, his father, / he will indeed carry it out by the force of what is destined to be, O honor-giver.

2.30.s:
sa tu rājā mahābhāgo vṛddhānāṃ paryupāsitā /
dattātreyāddhareraṃśāllabdhabodho mahāmatiḥ //
2.30.d:
स तु राजा महाभागो वृद्धानां पर्युपासिता ।
दत्तात्रेयाद्धरेरंशाल्लब्धबोधो महामतिः ॥
2.30.m: Yet that king is highly fortunate, an attendant of the elders, / highly intelligent, having attained knowledge from Dattātreya, a portion of Hari,

2.30.s:
sākṣādbhakto mahātmā ca tadvadhe pātakaṃ bhavet /
evamuktvā mahārāja sa bhṛgurbrahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ /
yathāgataṃ yayau vidvānbhaviṣyatkālaparyayāt //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyābhāge tṛtīya
upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite triṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 30//
2.30.d:
साक्षाद्भक्तो महात्मा च तद्वधे पातकं भवेत् ।
एवमुक्त्वा महाराज स भृगुर्ब्रह्मणः सुतः ।
यथागतं ययौ विद्वान्भविष्यत्कालपर्ययात् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्याभागे तृतीय
उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते त्रिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 30॥
2.30.m:
a direct devotee and a great soul; there will be sin in slaying him.” / Having spoken thus, O great king, Bhṛgu, the son of Brahmā, / being wise, departed just as he had come, in accordance with the course of future time.

Thus ends the thirtieth chapter in the Bhārgavacarita, in the third Upoddhātapāda of the middle section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

2.31.s:
sagara uvāca
brahmaputra mahābhāga vada bhārgavaceṣṭitam /
yaccakāra mahāvīryyo rājñaḥ kruddho hi karmaṇā //
2.31.d:
सगर उवाच
ब्रह्मपुत्र महाभाग वद भार्गवचेष्टितम् ।
यच्चकार महावीर्य्यो राज्ञः क्रुद्धो हि कर्मणा ॥
2.31.m:
Sagara said:
“O fortunate son of Brahmā, describe the deeds of the Bhārgava, / which the one of great valor performed, enraged indeed by the king's action.”

2.31.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
gate tasminmahābhāge bhṛgo pitṛparāyaṇaḥ /
rāmaḥ provāca saṃkruddho muñcañchvāsānmuharmuhuḥ //
2.31.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
गते तस्मिन्महाभागे भृगो पितृपरायणः ।
रामः प्रोवाच संक्रुद्धो मुञ्चञ्छ्वासान्मुहर्मुहुः ॥
2.31.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
When that fortunate Bhṛgu had gone, Rāma, devoted to his father, / spoke, enraged, sighing heavily again and again.

2.31.s:
paraśurāma uvāca
aho paśyata mūḍhatvaṃrājño hyutpathagāminaḥ /
kārttavīryasya yo vidvāṃścakre brahmavadhodyamam //
2.31.d:
परशुराम उवाच
अहो पश्यत मूढत्वंराज्ञो ह्युत्पथगामिनः ।
कार्त्तवीर्यस्य यो विद्वांश्चक्रे ब्रह्मवधोद्यमम् ॥
2.31.m:
Paraśurāma said:
“Ah, behold the foolishness of the king who strays from the proper path, / of Kārttavīrya who, though learned, undertook to kill a brāhmaṇa!

2.31.s:
daivaṃ hi balavanmanye yatprabhāvāccharīriṇaḥ /
śubhaṃ vāpyaśubhaṃ sarve prakurvanti vimohitāḥ //
2.31.d:
दैवं हि बलवन्मन्ये यत्प्रभावाच्छरीरिणः ।
शुभं वाप्यशुभं सर्वे प्रकुर्वन्ति विमोहिताः ॥
2.31.m: Indeed I deem fate to be powerful, through whose influence embodied beings, / all deluded, perform what is auspicious or inauspicious.

2.31.s:
śṛṇavantu ṛṣayaḥ sarve pratijñā kriyate mayā /
kārttavīryaṃ nihatyājau piturvairaṃ prasādhaye //
2.31.d:
शृणवन्तु ऋषयः सर्वे प्रतिज्ञा क्रियते मया ।
कार्त्तवीर्यं निहत्याजौ पितुर्वैरं प्रसाधये ॥
2.31.m: Let all the ṛṣis hear the vow made by me: / Having slain Kārttavīrya in battle, I will avenge my father.

2.31.s:
yadi rājā suraiḥ sarvairindrāddairdānavaistathā /
rakṣiṣyate tathāpyenaṃ saṃhariṣyāmi nānyathā //
2.31.d:
यदि राजा सुरैः सर्वैरिन्द्राद्दैर्दानवैस्तथा ।
रक्षिष्यते तथाप्येनं संहरिष्यामि नान्यथा ॥
2.31.m: Even if the king is protected by all the gods headed by Indra and by the dānavas, / nevertheless I will destroy him, not otherwise!”

2.31.s:
evamuktaṃ samākarṇya rāmeṇa samuhātmanā /
jamadagniruvācedaṃ putraṃ sāhasabhāṣiṇam //
2.31.d:
एवमुक्तं समाकर्ण्य रामेण समुहात्मना ।
जमदग्निरुवाचेदं पुत्रं साहसभाषिणम् ॥
2.31.m: Hearing this spoken by the high-souled Rāma, / Jamadagni said this to his son who spoke with audacity:

2.31.s:
jamadagniruvāca
śruṇu rāma pravakṣyāmi satāṃ dharmaṃ sanātanam /
yacchrutvā mānavāḥ sarve jāyante dharmakāriṇaḥ //
2.31.d:
जमदग्निरुवाच
श्रुणु राम प्रवक्ष्यामि सतां धर्मं सनातनम् ।
यच्छ्रुत्वा मानवाः सर्वे जायन्ते धर्मकारिणः ॥
2.31.m:
Jamadagni said:
“Listen, Rāma, I will tell the eternal dharma of the virtuous, / hearing which all mortals become performers of righteousness.

2.31.s:
sādhavo ye mahābhāgāḥ saṃsārānmokṣakāṅkṣiṇāḥ /
na kasmaicitprakupyanti ninditāstāḍitā api //
2.31.d:
साधवो ये महाभागाः संसारान्मोक्षकाङ्क्षिणाः ।
न कस्मैचित्प्रकुप्यन्ति निन्दितास्ताडिता अपि ॥
2.31.m: Those virtuous, highly fortunate ones who desire liberation from the cycle of existence / do not become angry at anyone, even when insulted or beaten.

2.31.s:
kṣamādhanā mahābhāgā ye ca dāntāstapasvinaḥ /
teṣāṃ caivākṣayā lokāḥ satataṃ sādhukāriṇām //
2.31.d:
क्षमाधना महाभागा ये च दान्तास्तपस्विनः ।
तेषां चैवाक्षया लोकाः सततं साधुकारिणाम् ॥
2.31.m: Those whose wealth is patience, the highly fortunate, self-controlled ascetics— / imperishable worlds belong to those who ever do what is good.

2.31.s:
yastu duṣṭaistu daṇḍādyairvacasāpi ca tāḍitaḥ /
na ca kṣobhamavāpnoti sa sādhuḥ parikīrtthate //
2.31.d:
यस्तु दुष्टैस्तु दण्डाद्यैर्वचसापि च ताडितः ।
न च क्षोभमवाप्नोति स साधुः परिकीर्त्थते ॥
2.31.m: He who, though struck by the wicked with sticks and the like, or even with words, / does not become agitated, is proclaimed to be virtuous.

2.31.s:
tāḍayettāḍayantaṃ yo na ca sādhuḥ sa pāpabhāk /
kṣamayār'haṇatāṃ prāptāḥ sādhavo brāhmaṇā vayam //
2.31.d:
ताडयेत्ताडयन्तं यो न च साधुः स पापभाक् ।
क्षमयार्ऽहणतां प्राप्ताः साधवो ब्राह्मणा वयम् ॥
2.31.m: He who strikes back at one who strikes is not virtuous; he incurs sin. / Through forgiveness we virtuous brāhmaṇas have attained worshipfulness.

2.31.s:
naranāthavadhe tāta pātakaṃ sumahadbhavet /
tasmānnivāraye tvādya kṣamāṃ kuru tapaścara //
2.31.d:
नरनाथवधे तात पातकं सुमहद्भवेत् ।
तस्मान्निवारये त्वाद्य क्षमां कुरु तपश्चर ॥
2.31.m: In the slaying of a ruler of men, my son, there would be a very great sin. / Therefore I restrain you today: practice patience and perform asceticism!”

2.31.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
evaṃ pitrā samādiṣṭaṃ vijñāya nṛpanandana /
rāmaḥ provāca pitaraṃ kṣamāśīlamarindamam //
2.31.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
एवं पित्रा समादिष्टं विज्ञाय नृपनन्दन ।
रामः प्रोवाच पितरं क्षमाशीलमरिन्दमम् ॥
2.31.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
Understanding what was thus instructed by his father, O prince, / Rāma spoke to his father, the subduer of foes whose nature was forgiveness:

2.31.s:
paraśurāma uvāca
śṛṇu tāta mahāprājña vi5ptiṃ mama sāṃpratam /
bhavatā śama uddiṣṭaḥ sādhūnāṃ sumahātmanām //
2.31.d:
परशुराम उवाच
शृणु तात महाप्राज्ञ वि5प्तिं मम सांप्रतम् ।
भवता शम उद्दिष्टः साधूनां सुमहात्मनाम् ॥
2.31.m:
Paraśurāma said:
“Listen, my dear father of great wisdom, to my petition now. / Peace has been taught by you for virtuous, high-souled men.

2.31.s:
ma śamaḥ sādhudīneṣu guruṣvīśvarabhāvanaiḥ /
karttavyo duṣṭaceṣṭeṣu na śamaḥ sukhado bhavet //
2.31.d:
म शमः साधुदीनेषु गुरुष्वीश्वरभावनैः ।
कर्त्तव्यो दुष्टचेष्टेषु न शमः सुखदो भवेत् ॥
2.31.m: Peace should be observed toward the good, the poor, and teachers, with the feeling of the Lord; / toward those of wicked deeds, peace would not bring happiness.

2.31.s:
tasmādasya vadhaḥ kāryaḥ kārttavīryasya vai mayā /
dehyājñāṃ mānanīyādya sādhaye vairamātmanaḥ //
2.31.d:
तस्मादस्य वधः कार्यः कार्त्तवीर्यस्य वै मया ।
देह्याज्ञां माननीयाद्य साधये वैरमात्मनः ॥
2.31.m: Therefore, the slaying of this Kārttavīrya must indeed be done by me. / Give your permission today, O venerable one; let me avenge myself!”

2.31.s:
jamadagniruvāca
śṛṇu rāma mahābhāga vaco mama samāhitaḥ /
kariṣyasi yathā bhāvi tathā naivānyathā bhavet //
2.31.d:
जमदग्निरुवाच
शृणु राम महाभाग वचो मम समाहितः ।
करिष्यसि यथा भावि तथा नैवान्यथा भवेत् ॥
2.31.m:
Jamadagni said:
“Listen with attention, O fortunate Rāma, to my words: / You will do what is destined to be, so it cannot happen otherwise.

2.31.s:
ito vrajatvaṃ brahmāṇāṃ bṛccha tāta hitāhitam /
sa yadvadiṣyati vibhustatkarttā nātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.31.d:
इतो व्रजत्वं ब्रह्माणां बृच्छ तात हिताहितम् ।
स यद्वदिष्यति विभुस्तत्कर्त्ता नात्र संशयः ॥
2.31.m: Go from here to Brahmā and ask him, my son, what is beneficial and what is harmful. / Whatever that sovereign lord says, that you will do, no doubt.”

2.31.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
evamuktaḥ sa pitaraṃ namaskṛtya mahāmatiḥ /
jagāma brahmaṇo lokamagamyaṃ prākṛtairjanaiḥ //
2.31.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
एवमुक्तः स पितरं नमस्कृत्य महामतिः ।
जगाम ब्रह्मणो लोकमगम्यं प्राकृतैर्जनैः ॥
2.31.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
Thus spoken to, the wise one, having bowed to his father, / went to the world of Brahmā, inaccessible to ordinary men.

2.31.s:
dadarśa brahmaṇo lokaṃ śātakaiṃbhavinirmitam /
svarṇaprākārasaṃyuktaṃ maṇistaṃbhairvimūṣitam //
2.31.d:
ददर्श ब्रह्मणो लोकं शातकैंभविनिर्मितम् ।
स्वर्णप्राकारसंयुक्तं मणिस्तंभैर्विमूषितम् ॥
2.31.m: He saw the world of Brahmā made of gold, / endowed with golden ramparts and adorned with jeweled pillars.

2.31.s:
tatrāpaśyatsamāsīnaṃ brahmāṇamamitaujasam /
ratnasiṃhāsane ramye ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam //
2.31.d:
तत्रापश्यत्समासीनं ब्रह्माणममितौजसम् ।
रत्नसिंहासने रम्ये रत्नभूषणभूषितम् ॥
2.31.m: There he saw Brahmā seated, possessed of immeasurable splendor, / on a delightful jeweled throne, adorned with gem-encrusted ornaments,

2.31.s:
siddhendraiśca munīndraiśca veṣṭitaṃ dhyānatatparaiḥ /
vidyādharīṇāṃ nṛtyaṃ ca paśyantaṃ sasmitaṃ mudā //
2.31.d:
सिद्धेन्द्रैश्च मुनीन्द्रैश्च वेष्टितं ध्यानतत्परैः ।
विद्याधरीणां नृत्यं च पश्यन्तं सस्मितं मुदा ॥
2.31.m: surrounded by lords of siddhas and lords of sages intent on meditation, / smiling with joy as he watched the dance of the vidyādharġs,

2.31.s:
tapasā phaladātāraṃ karttāraṃ jagatāṃ vibhum /
paripūrṇatamaṃ brahma dhyāyataṃ yatamānasam //
2.31.d:
तपसा फलदातारं कर्त्तारं जगतां विभुम् ।
परिपूर्णतमं ब्रह्म ध्यायतं यतमानसम् ॥
2.31.m: the giver of the fruits of asceticism, the maker and all-pervading lord of the worlds, / his mind restrained as he contemplated the most absolute Brahman,

2.31.s:
guhyayogaṃ pravocantaṃ bhaktavṛndeṣu saṃtatam /
dṛṣṭvā tamavyayaṃ bhaktyā praṇanāma bhṛgūdvahaḥ //
2.31.d:
गुह्ययोगं प्रवोचन्तं भक्तवृन्देषु संततम् ।
दृष्ट्वा तमव्ययं भक्त्या प्रणनाम भृगूद्वहः ॥
2.31.m: constantly expounding secret yoga among the hosts of devotees. / Having seen that imperishable one, the scion of Bhṛgu bowed down with devotion.

2.31.s:
sa dṛṣṭvā vinataṃ rāmamāśīrbhirabhinandya ca /
papraccha kuśalaṃ vatsa kathamāgamanaṃ kṛthāḥ //
2.31.d:
स दृष्ट्वा विनतं राममाशीर्भिरभिनन्द्य च ।
पप्रच्छ कुशलं वत्स कथमागमनं कृथाः ॥
2.31.m: Having seen Rāma bowed down and greeting him with blessings, / he asked after his welfare: “Child, why have you come?”

2.31.s:
saṃpṛṣṭo vidhinā rāmaḥ provācākhilamāditaḥ /
vṛttāntaṃ kārttavīryasya pituḥ svasya mahātmanaḥ //
2.31.d:
संपृष्टो विधिना रामः प्रोवाचाखिलमादितः ।
वृत्तान्तं कार्त्तवीर्यस्य पितुः स्वस्य महात्मनः ॥
2.31.m: Questioned by the Creator, Rāma related everything from the beginning: / the story of Kārttavġryārjuna and of his own noble father.

2.31.s:
tacchrutvā sakalaṃ brahmā vijñātārtho 'pi mānada /
uvāca rāmaṃ dharmiṣṭhaṃ pariṇāmasukhāvaham //
2.31.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा सकलं ब्रह्मा विज्ञातार्थो ऽपि मानद ।
उवाच रामं धर्मिष्ठं परिणामसुखावहम् ॥
2.31.m: Hearing all that, O giver of honor, Brahmā, though he already knew the matter, / spoke to the most righteous Rāma words bringing ultimate happiness:

2.31.s:
pratijñā durlabhā vatsa yāṃ bhavankṛtavānruṣā /
sṛṣṭi reṣā bhagavataḥ saṃbhavetkṛpayā baṭo //
2.31.d:
प्रतिज्ञा दुर्लभा वत्स यां भवन्कृतवान्रुषा ।
सृष्टि रेषा भगवतः संभवेत्कृपया बटो ॥
2.31.m: “Difficult is the vow, my child, which you have made in anger; / this creation of the Lord came to be through compassion, O boy.

2.31.s:
jagatsṛṣṭaṃ mayā tāta saṃkleśena tadājñayā /
tannāśakāriṇī caiva pratijñā bhavatā kṛtā //
2.31.d:
जगत्सृष्टं मया तात संक्लेशेन तदाज्ञया ।
तन्नाशकारिणी चैव प्रतिज्ञा भवता कृता ॥
2.31.m: The world was created by me, dear child, with great effort at his command; / yet a vow has been taken by you to destroy it.

2.31.s:
triḥsaptakṛtvo nirbhūpāṃ kartumicchasi medinīm /
ekasya rājño doṣeṇa pituḥ paribhavena ca //
2.31.d:
त्रिःसप्तकृत्वो निर्भूपां कर्तुमिच्छसि मेदिनीम् ।
एकस्य राज्ञो दोषेण पितुः परिभवेन च ॥
2.31.m: Three times seven times you wish to rid the earth of kings / on account of the fault of a single king and the humiliation of your father.

2.31.s:
brahmakṣatrriyaviṭśūdraiḥ sṛṣṭireṣā sanātanī /
āvirbhūtā tirobhūtā harereva punaḥ punaḥ //
2.31.d:
ब्रह्मक्षत्र्रियविट्शूद्रैः सृष्टिरेषा सनातनी ।
आविर्भूता तिरोभूता हरेरेव पुनः पुनः ॥
2.31.m: This eternal creation consisting of brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśhyas, and śūdras / is manifested and dissolved again and again by Hari alone.

2.31.s:
avyarthā tvatpratijñā tu bhavitrī prāktanena ca /
yadvāyāsena te kāryasiddhirbhavitumarhati //
2.31.d:
अव्यर्था त्वत्प्रतिज्ञा तु भवित्री प्राक्तनेन च ।
यद्वायासेन ते कार्यसिद्धिर्भवितुमर्हति ॥
2.31.m: Yet your vow will not be in vain, due to past karma, / or rather, through effort, your undertaking may achieve success.

2.31.s:
śivalokaṃ prayāhi tvaṃ śivasyājñāmavāpnuhi /
pṛthivyāṃ bahavo bhūpāḥ saṃti śaṅkarakiṅkarāḥ //
2.31.d:
शिवलोकं प्रयाहि त्वं शिवस्याज्ञामवाप्नुहि ।
पृथिव्यां बहवो भूपाः संति शङ्करकिङ्कराः ॥
2.31.m: Go to the realm of Śiva and obtain the command of Śiva; / on earth there are many kings who are servants of Śankara.

2.31.s:
vinaivājñāṃ maheśasya ko vā tānhantumīśvaraḥ /
bibhrataḥ kavacānyaṅge śaktīścāpi durāsadāḥ //
2.31.d:
विनैवाज्ञां महेशस्य को वा तान्हन्तुमीश्वरः ।
बिभ्रतः कवचान्यङ्गे शक्तीश्चापि दुरासदाः ॥
2.31.m: Without the very command of the great lord, who indeed is capable of slaying them, / clad as they are in armors and bearing powers hard to overcome?

2.31.s:
upāyaṃ kuru yatnena jayabījaṃ śubhāvaham /
upāye tu samārabdhe sarve sidhyantyupakramāḥ //
2.31.d:
उपायं कुरु यत्नेन जयबीजं शुभावहम् ।
उपाये तु समारब्धे सर्वे सिध्यन्त्युपक्रमाः ॥
2.31.m: Diligently adopt an expedient, the auspicious seed of victory; / for when an expedient is undertaken, all endeavors succeed.

2.31.s:
śrīkṛṣṇamantraṃ kavacaṃ gṛhṇa vatsa gurorharāt /
durllaṅghyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tejaḥ śivaśaktirvijeṣyati //
2.31.d:
श्रीकृष्णमन्त्रं कवचं गृह्ण वत्स गुरोर्हरात् ।
दुर्ल्लङ्घ्यं वैष्णवं तेजः शिवशक्तिर्विजेष्यति ॥
2.31.m: Receive, my child, from your guru Hara the mantra of Śrikṛṣṇa and the armor; / the impassable Vaiṣṇava energy, combined with Śiva’s power, will conquer.

2.31.s:
trailokyavijayaṃ nāma kavacaṃ paramādbhutam /
yathākathaṃ ca vijñāpya śaṅkaraṃ labhadurlabham //
2.31.d:
त्रैलोक्यविजयं नाम कवचं परमाद्भुतम् ।
यथाकथं च विज्ञाप्य शङ्करं लभदुर्लभम् ॥
2.31.m: It is the most wondrous armor named Trailokyavijaya; / by any means petitioning Śankara, obtain that which is difficult to attain.

2.31.s:
prasannaḥ sa guṇaistubhyaṃ kṛpālurdīnavatsalaḥ /
divyapāśupataṃ cāpi dāsyatyeva na saṃśayaḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya
upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite ekatriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 31//
2.31.d:
प्रसन्नः स गुणैस्तुभ्यं कृपालुर्दीनवत्सलः ।
दिव्यपाशुपतं चापि दास्यत्येव न संशयः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय
उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते एकत्रिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 31॥
2.31.m:
Pleased with your virtues, compassionate, and fond of the wretched, / he will surely grant you the divine Pāśupata weapon as well, no doubt.”

Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the story of the scion of Bhṛgu in the Upoddhātapāda, the third part of the middle section of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu. // 31

2.32.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā sa praṇamya jagadgurum /
prasannacetāḥ subhṛśaṃ śivalokaṃ jagāma ha //
2.32.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
ब्रह्मणो वचनं श्रुत्वा स प्रणम्य जगद्गुरुम् ।
प्रसन्नचेताः सुभृशं शिवलोकं जगाम ह ॥
2.32.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Hearing the word of Brahmā and having bowed to the teacher of the world, / with a greatly delighted mind he went indeed to the realm of Śiva,

2.32.s:
lakṣayojanamūrddhvaṃ ca brahmalokā dvilakṣaṇam /
athanirvacanīyaṃ ca yogigamyaṃ parātparam //
2.32.d:
लक्षयोजनमूर्द्ध्वं च ब्रह्मलोका द्विलक्षणम् ।
अथनिर्वचनीयं च योगिगम्यं परात्परम् ॥
2.32.m: a hundred thousand yojanas above Brahmā’s realm and distinct [from it], / inexpressible, accessible to yogins, higher than the highest,

2.32.s:
vaikuṇṭho dakṣiṇe yasmādgaurīlokaśca vāmataḥ /
yadadho dhruvalokaśca sarvalokaparastu saḥ //
2.32.d:
वैकुण्ठो दक्षिणे यस्माद्गौरीलोकश्च वामतः ।
यदधो ध्रुवलोकश्च सर्वलोकपरस्तु सः ॥
2.32.m: to the right of which is Vaikuṇṭha and to the left the realm of Gaurī, / below which is the realm of Dhruva, and which is superior to all realms.

2.32.s:
tapovīryagatī rāmaḥ śivalokaṃ dadarśa ca /
upamānena rahitaṃ nānākautukasaṃyutam //
2.32.d:
तपोवीर्यगती रामः शिवलोकं ददर्श च ।
उपमानेन रहितं नानाकौतुकसंयुतम् ॥
2.32.m: Reaching it by the power of his asceticism, Rāma beheld the realm of Śiva, / devoid of comparison and filled with various wonders,

2.32.s:
vasaṃti yatra yogīndrāḥ siddhāḥ pāśupatāḥ śubhāḥ /
koṭikalpatapaḥ puṇyāḥ śāntā nirmatsarā janāḥ //
2.32.d:
वसंति यत्र योगीन्द्राः सिद्धाः पाशुपताः शुभाः ।
कोटिकल्पतपः पुण्याः शान्ता निर्मत्सरा जनाः ॥
2.32.m: where dwell lords of yogins, siddhas, auspicious Pāśupatas, / peaceful, un-envious people whose merit is the asceticism of a crore of kalpas;

2.32.s:
pārijātamukhairvṛkṣaiḥ śobhitaṃ kāmadhenubhiḥ /
yogena yoginā sṛṣṭaṃ svecchayā śaṅkareṇa hi //
2.32.d:
पारिजातमुखैर्वृक्षैः शोभितं कामधेनुभिः ।
योगेन योगिना सृष्टं स्वेच्छया शङ्करेण हि ॥
2.32.m: adorned with trees led by pārijātas and with wishes-granting cows; / created through yoga by the yogin Śankara by his own will,

2.32.s:
śilpināṃ guruṇā svapne na dṛṣṭaṃ niśvakarmaṇā /
sarovaraśatairdivyaiḥ padmarāgavirājitaiḥ //
2.32.d:
शिल्पिनां गुरुणा स्वप्ने न दृष्टं निश्वकर्मणा ।
सरोवरशतैर्दिव्यैः पद्मरागविराजितैः ॥
2.32.m: not seen even in dream by Viśvakarman, the teacher of artisans; / with hundreds of divine lakes shining with rubies,

2.32.s:
śobhitaṃ cātiramyaṃ ca saṃyuktaṃ maṇivedibhiḥ /
suvarṇaratnaracitaprākāreṇa samāvṛtam //
2.32.d:
शोभितं चातिरम्यं च संयुक्तं मणिवेदिभिः ।
सुवर्णरत्नरचितप्राकारेण समावृतम् ॥
2.32.m: adorned and exceedingly delightful, provided with gem-set platforms, / surrounded by an enclosure wall made of gold and jewels,

2.32.s:
atyūrddhvamaṃbarasparśi svacchaṃ kṣīranibhaṃparam /
caturdvārasamāyuktaṃ śobhitaṃ maṇivedibhiḥ //
2.32.d:
अत्यूर्द्ध्वमंबरस्पर्शि स्वच्छं क्षीरनिभंपरम् ।
चतुर्द्वारसमायुक्तं शोभितं मणिवेदिभिः ॥
2.32.m: exceedingly high, touching the sky, clear, resembling milk, supreme, / furnished with four gates and adorned with gem-set platforms,

2.32.s:
raktasopānayuktaiśca ratnastaṃbhakapāṭakaiḥ /
nānācitravicitraiśca śobhitaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ //
2.32.d:
रक्तसोपानयुक्तैश्च रत्नस्तंभकपाटकैः ।
नानाचित्रविचित्रैश्च शोभितैः सुमनोहरैः ॥
2.32.m: with red staircases, and jewel-pillared doorways / adorned with various colorful and very charming [decorations].

2.32.s:
tanmadhaye bhavanaṃ ramyaṃ siṃhadvāropaśobhitam /
dadarśarāmo dharmātmā vicitramiva saṃgataḥ //
2.32.d:
तन्मधये भवनं रम्यं सिंहद्वारोपशोभितम् ।
ददर्शरामो धर्मात्मा विचित्रमिव संगतः ॥
2.32.m: In the midst of it, the righteous Rāma saw a delightful mansion / adorned with a lion-gate, resembling a wondrous assembly.

2.32.s:
tatra sthitau dvāra pālau dadarśātibhayaṅkarau /
mahākarāladantāsyau vikṛtāraktalocanau //
2.32.d:
तत्र स्थितौ द्वार पालौ ददर्शातिभयङ्करौ ।
महाकरालदन्तास्यौ विकृतारक्तलोचनौ ॥
2.32.m: There he beheld two gatekeepers standing, exceedingly terrifying, / their faces having huge, dreadful teeth, with deformed, reddish eyes,

2.32.s:
dagdhaśailapratīkāśau mahābalaparākramau /
vibhūtibhūṣitāṅgau ca vyāghracarmāṃbarau ca tau //
2.32.d:
दग्धशैलप्रतीकाशौ महाबलपराक्रमौ ।
विभूतिभूषिताङ्गौ च व्याघ्रचर्मांबरौ च तौ ॥
2.32.m: resembling burnt mountains, of mighty strength and valor, / their limbs smeared with sacred ash, and clad in garments of tiger-skin,

2.32.s:
triśūlapaṭṭiśadharau jvalantau brahmatejasā /
tau dṛṣṭvā manasā bhītaḥ kiñcidāha vinītavat //
2.32.d:
त्रिशूलपट्टिशधरौ ज्वलन्तौ ब्रह्मतेजसा ।
तौ दृष्ट्वा मनसा भीतः किञ्चिदाह विनीतवत् ॥
2.32.m: bearing tridents and sharp spears, blazing with brāhmaṇical radiance. / Seeing the two, frightened in mind, he spoke somewhat humbly:

2.32.s:
namaskaromi vāmīśau śaṅkaraṃ draṣṭumāgataḥ /
īśvarājñāṃ samādāya māmathājñaptumarhatha //
2.32.d:
नमस्करोमि वामीशौ शङ्करं द्रष्टुमागतः ।
ईश्वराज्ञां समादाय मामथाज्ञप्तुमर्हथ ॥
2.32.m: “My obeisance to both of you, O masters; I have come to behold Śankara. / Taking the Lord’s command, you ought now to direct me.”

2.32.s:
tautu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā gṛhītvājñāṃ śivasya ca /
praveṣṭumājñāṃ dadaturīśvarānucarau ca tau //
2.32.d:
तौतु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा गृहीत्वाज्ञां शिवस्य च ।
प्रवेष्टुमाज्ञां ददतुरीश्वरानुचरौ च तौ ॥
2.32.m: Hearing his words, those two attendants of the Lord, / having obtained Śiva’s permission, granted him permission to enter.

2.32.s:
sa tadājñāmanuprāpya viveśāntaḥ puraṃ mudā /
tatrātiramyāṃ siddhaughaiḥ samākīrṇāṃ sabhāṃ dvijaḥ //
2.32.d:
स तदाज्ञामनुप्राप्य विवेशान्तः पुरं मुदा ।
तत्रातिरम्यां सिद्धौघैः समाकीर्णां सभां द्विजः ॥
2.32.m: Having obtained their permission, he joyfully entered the inner quarters; / there the twice-born saw the Lord’s exceedingly delightful assembly,

2.32.s:
dṛṣṭvā vismayamāpede sugandhabahulāṃ vibhoḥ /
tatrāpaśyacchivaṃ śāntaṃ trinetraṃ candraśekharam //
2.32.d:
दृष्ट्वा विस्मयमापेदे सुगन्धबहुलां विभोः ।
तत्रापश्यच्छिवं शान्तं त्रिनेत्रं चन्द्रशेखरम् ॥
2.32.m: filled with hosts of siddhas, rich with fragrance, and was filled with wonder. / There he beheld the peaceful Śiva, three-eyed, crescent-crested,

2.32.s:
triśūlaśobhitakaraṃ vyāghracarmavarāṃbaram /
vibhūtibhūṣitāṅgaṃ ca nāgayajñopavītinam //
2.32.d:
त्रिशूलशोभितकरं व्याघ्रचर्मवरांबरम् ।
विभूतिभूषिताङ्गं च नागयज्ञोपवीतिनम् ॥
2.32.m: his hand adorned with a trident, clad in an excellent tiger-skin garment, / his limbs smeared with sacred ash, having a serpent as his sacred thread,

2.32.s:
ātmārāmaṃ pūrṇakāmaṃ koṭisūryasamaprabham /
pañcānanaṃ daśabhujaṃ bhaktānugrahavigraham //
2.32.d:
आत्मारामं पूर्णकामं कोटिसूर्यसमप्रभम् ।
पञ्चाननं दशभुजं भक्तानुग्रहविग्रहम् ॥
2.32.m: delighting in the Self, whose desires are fulfilled, with the luster of a crore of suns, / five-faced, ten-armed, the embodiment of grace toward his devotees,

2.32.s:
yogajñāne prabruvantaṃ siddhebhyastarkamudrayā /
stūyamānaṃ ca yokīndraiḥ pramathaprakarairmudā //
2.32.d:
योगज्ञाने प्रब्रुवन्तं सिद्धेभ्यस्तर्कमुद्रया ।
स्तूयमानं च योकीन्द्रैः प्रमथप्रकरैर्मुदा ॥
2.32.m: expounding knowledge of yoga to the siddhas with the gesture of disputation, / being praised with joy by lords of yogins and multitudes of Pramathas,

2.32.s:
bhairavairyoginībhiśca vṛtaṃ rudragaṇaistathā /
mūrdhnā namāma taṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ paramayā mudā //
2.32.d:
भैरवैर्योगिनीभिश्च वृतं रुद्रगणैस्तथा ।
मूर्ध्ना नमाम तं दृष्ट्वा रामः परमया मुदा ॥
2.32.m: surrounded by Bhairavas, yoginġs, and hosts of Rudras. / Seeing him, Rāma bowed down with his head in supreme joy.

2.32.s:
vāmabhāge kārttikeyaṃ dakṣiṇe ca gaṇeśvaram /
nandīśvaraṃ mahākālaṃ vīrabhadraṃ ca tatpuraḥ //
2.32.d:
वामभागे कार्त्तिकेयं दक्षिणे च गणेश्वरम् ।
नन्दीश्वरं महाकालं वीरभद्रं च तत्पुरः ॥
2.32.m: On his left side [he saw] Kārttikeya, and on his right Gaṇeśvara; / Nandīśvara, Mahākāla, and Vġrabhadra in front of him;

2.32.s:
kroḍe durgāṃ śatabhujāṃ dṛṣṭvā natvātha tāmapi /
stotuṃ pracakrame vidvāngirā gadgadayā vibhum //
2.32.d:
क्रोडे दुर्गां शतभुजां दृष्ट्वा नत्वाथ तामपि ।
स्तोतुं प्रचक्रमे विद्वान्गिरा गद्गदया विभुम् ॥
2.32.m: having seen also Durgā of a hundred arms upon his lap and bowed to her, / the learned one proceeded to praise the all-pervading Lord with a faltering voice:

2.32.s:
namasye śivamīśānaṃ vibhuṃ vyāpakamavyayam /
bhujaṅgabhūṣaṇaṃ cograṃ nṛkapālasragujjvalam //
2.32.d:
नमस्ये शिवमीशानं विभुं व्यापकमव्ययम् ।
भुजङ्गभूषणं चोग्रं नृकपालस्रगुज्ज्वलम् ॥
2.32.m: “ I bow to Śiva, the sovereign lord, the all-pervading, omnipresent, imperishable one, / adorned with serpents, fierce, resplendent with a garland of human skulls,

2.32.s:
yo vibhuḥ sarvalokānāṃ sṛṣṭisthitivināśakṛt /
brahmādirūpadhṛgjyeṣṭhastaṃ tvāṃ veda kṛpārṇavam //
2.32.d:
यो विभुः सर्वलोकानां सृष्टिस्थितिविनाशकृत् ।
ब्रह्मादिरूपधृग्ज्येष्ठस्तं त्वां वेद कृपार्णवम् ॥
2.32.m: who is the lord of all worlds, the maker of creation, preservation, and destruction, / assuming forms such as Brahmā, the eldest; I know you to be an ocean of compassion.

2.32.s:
vedā na śaktā yaṃ stotu mavāṅmanasagocaram /
jñānabuddhyorasādhyaṃ ca nirākāraṃ namāmyaham //
2.32.d:
वेदा न शक्ता यं स्तोतु मवाङ्मनसगोचरम् ।
ज्ञानबुद्ध्योरसाध्यं च निराकारं नमाम्यहम् ॥
2.32.m: Whom the Vedas are not able to praise, who is beyond the range of speech and mind, / unattainable by intellectual knowledge, and formless—to him I bow.

2.32.s:
śakrādayaḥ suragaṇā ṛṣayo manavo 'surāḥ /
na yaṃ viduryathātattvaṃ taṃ namāmi parātparam //
2.32.d:
शक्रादयः सुरगणा ऋषयो मनवो ऽसुराः ।
न यं विदुर्यथातत्त्वं तं नमामि परात्परम् ॥
2.32.m: Whom the host of gods led by Śakra, the ṛṣis, the Manus, and the asuras / do not know in his true reality—to that one, higher than the highest, I bow.”

2.32.s:
yasyāṃśāṃśena sṛjayante lokāḥ sarve carācarāḥ /
līyante ca punaryasmiṃstaṃ namāmi jaganmayam //
2.32.d:
यस्यांशांशेन सृजयन्ते लोकाः सर्वे चराचराः ।
लीयन्ते च पुनर्यस्मिंस्तं नमामि जगन्मयम् ॥
2.32.m: By a fraction of whose fraction all worlds, moving and unmoving, are created, / and into whom they dissolve again—to that one, who is the universe itself, I bow.

2.32.s:
yasyeṣatkopasaṃbhūto hutāśo dahate 'khilam /
sorddhvalokaṃ sapātālaṃ taṃ namāmi haraṃ param //
2.32.d:
यस्येषत्कोपसंभूतो हुताशो दहते ऽखिलम् ।
सोर्द्ध्वलोकं सपातालं तं नमामि हरं परम् ॥
2.32.m: From a slight [flicker] of whose wrath fire arises and consumes everything, / both the upper world and the nether regions—to that supreme Hara I bow.

2.32.s:
pṛthvīpavana vahnyabhabhonabhoyajvendubhāskarāḥ /
mūrttayo 'ṣṭau jagatpūjyāstaṃ yajñaṃ praṇamāmyaham //
2.32.d:
पृथ्वीपवन वह्न्यभभोनभोयज्वेन्दुभास्कराः ।
मूर्त्तयो ऽष्टौ जगत्पूज्यास्तं यज्ञं प्रणमाम्यहम् ॥
2.32.m: Earth, wind, fire, water, sky, sacrificer, moon, and sun— / these eight forms are adored by the world; to that sacrifice I bow down.

2.32.s:
yaḥ kālarūpo jagadādikarttā pātā pṛthagrūpadharo jaganmayaḥ /
rarttā punā rudravapustathānte taṃ kālarūpaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye //
2.32.d:
यः कालरूपो जगदादिकर्त्ता पाता पृथग्रूपधरो जगन्मयः ।
रर्त्ता पुना रुद्रवपुस्तथान्ते तं कालरूपं शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥
2.32.m: Who in the form of Time is the first creator of the universe, who in separate forms preserves it and embodies the universe, / and who at the end destroys it in the form of Rudra—to that one whose form is Time I fly for refuge.

2.32.s:
ityevamuktvā sa tu bhārgavo mudā paṣāta tasyāṅghri samīpa āturaḥ /
utthāpya taṃ vāmakareṇa līlayā dadhre tadā mūrdhni karaṃ kṛpārṇavaḥ //
2.32.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा स तु भार्गवो मुदा पषात तस्याङ्घ्रि समीप आतुरः ।
उत्थाप्य तं वामकरेण लीलया दध्रे तदा मूर्ध्नि करं कृपार्णवः ॥
2.32.m: Having spoken thus, the Bhārgava, distressed, fell with joy near his feet; / lifting him up playfully with his left hand, the ocean of compassion then placed his hand upon his head.

2.32.s:
āśīrbhirenaṃ hyabhinandya sādaraṃ niveśayāmāsa gaṇeśapūrvataḥ /
uvāca vāmāmabhivīkṣya cāpyumāṃ kṛpārdradṛṣṭyākhilakāmapūrakaḥ //
2.32.d:
आशीर्भिरेनं ह्यभिनन्द्य सादरं निवेशयामास गणेशपूर्वतः ।
उवाच वामामभिवीक्ष्य चाप्युमां कृपार्द्रदृष्ट्याखिलकामपूरकः ॥
2.32.m: Congratulating him respectfully with blessings, he seated him in front of Gaṇeśa; / and looking upon Umā, seated at his left, with a gaze moist with compassion, he who fulfills all desires spoke:

2.32.s:
śiva uvāca
kastvaṃ vaṭo kasyakule prasūtaḥ kiṃ kāryamuddiśya bhavānihāgataḥ /
vinirddiśāhaṃ tava bhaktibhāvataḥ prītaḥ pradadyāṃ bhavato manogatam //
2.32.d:
शिव उवाच
कस्त्वं वटो कस्यकुले प्रसूतः किं कार्यमुद्दिश्य भवानिहागतः ।
विनिर्द्दिशाहं तव भक्तिभावतः प्रीतः प्रदद्यां भवतो मनोगतम् ॥
2.32.m: Śiva said: / Who are you, young man? In whose family were you born? For what purpose have you come here? / Explain; pleased with your devotion, I shall grant what is in your heart.

2.32.s:
ityevamuktaḥ sa bhṛgurmahātmanā hareṇa viśvārttihareṇa sādaram /
punaśca natvā vibudhāṃ pati guruṃ kṛpāsamudraṃ samuvāca satvaram //
2.32.d:
इत्येवमुक्तः स भृगुर्महात्मना हरेण विश्वार्त्तिहरेण सादरम् ।
पुनश्च नत्वा विबुधां पति गुरुं कृपासमुद्रं समुवाच सत्वरम् ॥
2.32.m: Addressed in this manner with respect by the great-souled Hara, who removes the distress of the universe, / having bowed again to the lord of the gods, the guru, the ocean of compassion, Bhṛgu's descendant promptly said:

2.32.s:
paraśurāma uvāca
bhṛgoścāhaṃ kule jāto jamadagnisutau vibho /
rāmo nāma jagadvandyaṃ tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
2.32.d:
परशुराम उवाच
भृगोश्चाहं कुले जातो जमदग्निसुतौ विभो ।
रामो नाम जगद्वन्द्यं त्वामहं शरणं गतः ॥
2.32.m: Paraśurāma said: / I was born in the lineage of Bhṛgu, O lord, as a son of Jamadagni; / named Rāma, I have come for refuge to you who are praised by the whole world.

2.32.s:
yatkāryārthamahaṃ nātha tava sāṃnidhyamāgataḥ /
taṃ prasādhaya viśveśa vāñchitaṃ kāmameva me //
2.32.d:
यत्कार्यार्थमहं नाथ तव सांनिध्यमागतः ।
तं प्रसाधय विश्वेश वाञ्छितं काममेव मे ॥
2.32.m: O lord, the purpose for which I have come into your presence— / accomplish that very desired wish of mine, O ruler of the universe!

2.32.s:
mṛgayāmāgatasyāpi kārttavīryasya bhūpateḥ /
ātithyaṃ kṛtavān deva jamadagniḥ pitā mama //
2.32.d:
मृगयामागतस्यापि कार्त्तवीर्यस्य भूपतेः ।
आतिथ्यं कृतवान् देव जमदग्निः पिता मम ॥
2.32.m: When King Kārttavīrya came on a hunt, / my father Jamadagni offered him hospitality, O god.

2.32.s:
rājā taṃ sa balāllobhātpātayāmāsa mandadhīḥ /
sā dhenustaṃ mṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā gavāṃ lokaṃ jagāma ha //
2.32.d:
राजा तं स बलाल्लोभात्पातयामास मन्दधीः ।
सा धेनुस्तं मृतं दृष्ट्वा गवां लोकं जगाम ह ॥
2.32.m: Through greed and by force, that dull-witted king struck him down; / seeing him dead, that cow went away to the world of cows.

2.32.s:
rājā na śocanmaraṇaṃ piturmama nirāgasaḥ /
jagāma svapuraṃ paścānmātā me prārudadbhṛśam //
2.32.d:
राजा न शोचन्मरणं पितुर्मम निरागसः ।
जगाम स्वपुरं पश्चान्माता मे प्रारुदद्भृशम् ॥
2.32.m: The king, not grieving the death of my guiltless father, / departed to his own city; afterwards, my mother wept bitterly.

2.32.s:
tajjñātvā lokavṛttajño bhṛgurnaḥ prapitāmahaḥ /
ājagāma mahādeva hyahamapyāgato vanāt //
2.32.d:
तज्ज्ञात्वा लोकवृत्तज्ञो भृगुर्नः प्रपितामहः ।
आजगाम महादेव ह्यहमप्यागतो वनात् ॥
2.32.m: Knowing that, Bhṛgu, our great-grandfather who knows worldly affairs, / came, O Mahādeva, and I too returned from the forest.

2.32.s:
mayā maha suduḥkhārttānbhrātṝnmātrāsahaiva me /
sāṃtvayitvā sa mantrajño 'jīvayatpitaraṃ mama //
2.32.d:
मया मह सुदुःखार्त्तान्भ्रातॄन्मात्रासहैव मे ।
सांत्वयित्वा स मन्त्रज्ञो ऽजीवयत्पितरं मम ॥
2.32.m: Consoling along with me my brothers and my mother, all stricken with deep sorrow, / he, knowing the mantras, brought my father back to life.

2.32.s:
ānāgate bhṛgau māturduḥkhenāhaṃ prakopitaḥ /
pratijñāṃ kṛtavāndeva sātvayanmātaraṃsvakām //
2.32.d:
आनागते भृगौ मातुर्दुःखेनाहं प्रकोपितः ।
प्रतिज्ञां कृतवान्देव सात्वयन्मातरंस्वकाम् ॥
2.32.m: Before Bhṛgu arrived, enraged by my mother's sorrow, / I made a vow, O god, consoling my mother:

2.32.s:
triḥsaptakṛtvo yadurastāḍitaṃ māturātmanaḥ /
tāvatsaṃkhyamahaṃ pṛthvīṃ kariṣye kṣatravarjitām //
2.32.d:
त्रिःसप्तकृत्वो यदुरस्ताडितं मातुरात्मनः ।
तावत्संख्यमहं पृथ्वीं करिष्ये क्षत्रवर्जिताम् ॥
2.32.m: ‘As many as twenty-one times as my mother’s breast was beaten, / that many times I shall rid the earth of kṣatriyas.’

2.32.s:
ityevaṃ paripūrṇā me karttā devo jagatpatiḥ /
mahādevo hyato nātha tvatsakāṇamihāgataḥ //
2.32.d:
इत्येवं परिपूर्णा मे कर्त्ता देवो जगत्पतिः ।
महादेवो ह्यतो नाथ त्वत्सकाणमिहागतः ॥
2.32.m: God, the lord of the universe, Mahādeva, will fulfill this [vow] for me; / therefore, O lord, I have come here to your presence.

2.32.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityevaṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā durgāmukhaṃ haraḥ /
babhūvānamravadanaschintayānaḥ kṣaṇaṃ tadā //
2.32.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्येवं तद्वचः श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा दुर्गामुखं हरः ।
बभूवानम्रवदनस्छिन्तयानः क्षणं तदा ॥
2.32.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having heard those words and looked upon Durgā’s face, / Hara bent his face downward and thought for a moment then.

2.32.s:
etasminnantare durgā vismitā prāhasadbhṛśam /
uvāca ca mahārāja bhārgavaṃ vairasādhakam //
2.32.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दुर्गा विस्मिता प्राहसद्भृशम् ।
उवाच च महाराज भार्गवं वैरसाधकम् ॥
2.32.m: Meanwhile Durgā, filled with wonder, laughed aloud, / and said, O great king, to the Bhārgava who sought his revenge:

2.32.s:
tapasvindvijaputra kṣmāṃ nirbhūpāṃ karttumicchasi /
triḥ saptakṛtvaḥ kopena sāhasaste mahānbaṭo //
2.32.d:
तपस्विन्द्विजपुत्र क्ष्मां निर्भूपां कर्त्तुमिच्छसि ।
त्रिः सप्तकृत्वः कोपेन साहसस्ते महान्बटो ॥
2.32.m: ‘O ascetic, son of a twice-born, you wish to make the earth kingless / twenty-one times in your anger! Great is your daring, O lad!

2.32.s:
hantumicchasi niḥśastraḥ sahasrārjunamīśvaram /
bhrūbhaṅgalīlayā yena rāvaṇo 'pi nirākṛtaḥ //
2.32.d:
हन्तुमिच्छसि निःशस्त्रः सहस्रार्जुनमीश्वरम् ।
भ्रूभङ्गलीलया येन रावणो ऽपि निराकृतः ॥
2.32.m: Weaponless, you wish to slay the lord Sahasrārjuna, / by whom even Rāvaṇa was defeated with a mere playful knit of his brow!

2.32.s:
tasmai pradattaṃ dattena śrīhareḥ kavacaṃ purā /
śaktiratyarthavīryā ca taṃ kathaṃ hantumicchasi //
2.32.d:
तस्मै प्रदत्तं दत्तेन श्रीहरेः कवचं पुरा ।
शक्तिरत्यर्थवीर्या च तं कथं हन्तुमिच्छसि ॥
2.32.m: Formerly, the armor of Śrī Hari was given to him by Datta, / and a spear of immense power; how do you wish to slay him?

2.32.s:
śaṅkaraḥ karuṇāsiddhaḥ karttuṃ cāpyanyathā vibhuḥ /
na cānyaḥ śaṅkarātputra satkāryaṃ karttumīśvaraḥ //
2.32.d:
शङ्करः करुणासिद्धः कर्त्तुं चाप्यन्यथा विभुः ।
न चान्यः शङ्करात्पुत्र सत्कार्यं कर्त्तुमीश्वरः ॥
2.32.m: Śaṅkara is perfected through compassion and is competent to alter this; / and none other than Śaṅkara, my son, has the power to achieve this good deed.’

2.32.s:
atha devyā anumatiṃ prāpya śaṃbhurddayārṇavaḥ /
abhyadhādbhadrayā vāyā jamadagnisutaṃ vibhuḥ //
2.32.d:
अथ देव्या अनुमतिं प्राप्य शंभुर्द्दयार्णवः ।
अभ्यधाद्भद्रया वाया जमदग्निसुतं विभुः ॥
2.32.m: Then, having obtained the assent of the Goddess, Śambhu, the ocean of mercy, the lord, / addressed the son of Jamadagni in auspicious speech:

2.32.s:
śiva uvāca
adyaprabhṛti vipra tvaṃ mama skandasamo bhava /
dāsyāmi mantraṃ divyaṃ te kavacaṃ ca mahāmate //
2.32.d:
शिव उवाच
अद्यप्रभृति विप्र त्वं मम स्कन्दसमो भव ।
दास्यामि मन्त्रं दिव्यं ते कवचं च महामते ॥
2.32.m: Śiva said: / From this day forward, O brāhmaṇa, be equal to my Skanda; / I shall give you a divine mantra and armor, O noble-minded one,

2.32.s:
līlayā yatprasādena kārttavīryaṃ haniṣyasi /
triḥ saptakṛtvo nirbhūpāṃ mahīṃ cāpi kariṣyasi //
2.32.d:
लीलया यत्प्रसादेन कार्त्तवीर्यं हनिष्यसि ।
त्रिः सप्तकृत्वो निर्भूपां महीं चापि करिष्यसि ॥
2.32.m: By the grace of which you will easily slay Kārttavīrya, / and make the earth kingless twenty-one times.

2.32.s:
ityuktvā śaṅkarastasmai dadau mantraṃ sudurlabham /
trailokyavijayaṃ nāma kavacaṃ paramādbhutam //
2.32.d:
इत्युक्त्वा शङ्करस्तस्मै ददौ मन्त्रं सुदुर्लभम् ।
त्रैलोक्यविजयं नाम कवचं परमाद्भुतम् ॥
2.32.m: Having spoken thus, Śaṅkara gave him a mantra very difficult to obtain, / and the wondrous armor named Trailokyavijaya [‘Victory over the Three Worlds’];

2.32.s:
nāgapāśaṃ pāśupataṃ brahmāstraṃ ca sudurllabham /
nārāyaṇāstramāgneyaṃ vāyavyaṃ vāruṇaṃ tathā //
2.32.d:
नागपाशं पाशुपतं ब्रह्मास्त्रं च सुदुर्ल्लभम् ।
नारायणास्त्रमाग्नेयं वायव्यं वारुणं तथा ॥
2.32.m: The serpent-noose, the pāśupata, and the brahmāstra very difficult to obtain, / the nārāyaṇāstra, the fiery weapon, the wind weapon, and likewise the water weapon,

2.32.s:
ghāndharvaṃ gāruḍaṃ caiva jṛṃbhaṇāstraṃ mahādbhutam /
gadāṃ śaktiṃ ca paraśuṃ śūlaṃ daṇḍamanuttamam //
2.32.d:
घान्धर्वं गारुडं चैव जृंभणास्त्रं महाद्भुतम् ।
गदां शक्तिं च परशुं शूलं दण्डमनुत्तमम् ॥
2.32.m: The gandharva weapon, the eagle weapon, and the wondrous weapon of stupor; / the mace, the spear, the battle-axe, the trident, and the peerless staff.

2.32.s:
śastrāstragrāmamakhilaṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ saṃbabhūva ha /
namaskṛtya śivaṃ śāntaṃ durgāṃ skandaṃ gaṇeśvaram //
2.32.d:
शस्त्रास्त्रग्राममखिलं प्रहृष्टः संबभूव ह ।
नमस्कृत्य शिवं शान्तं दुर्गां स्कन्दं गणेश्वरम् ॥
2.32.m: [Receiving] that entire array of weapons and missiles, he was filled with joy; / bowing to gentle Śiva, Durgā, Skanda, and the lord of the gaṇas,

2.32.s:
parikramya yayau rāmaḥ puṣkaraṃ tīrthamuttamam /
siddhaṃ kṛtvā śivoktaṃ tu mantraṃ kavacamuttamam //
2.32.d:
परिक्रम्य ययौ रामः पुष्करं तीर्थमुत्तमम् ।
सिद्धं कृत्वा शिवोक्तं तु मन्त्रं कवचमुत्तमम् ॥
2.32.m: And circumambulating them, Rāma went to the excellent sacred place Puṣkara; / and having mastered the excellent mantra and armor spoken by Śiva,

2.32.s:
sādhayāmāsa nikhilaṃ svakāryaṃ bhṛgunandanaḥ /
nihatya kārttavīryaṃ taṃ sasainyaṃ sakulaṃ mudā /
vinivṛtto gṛhaṃ prāgātpituḥ svasya bhṛgūdvahaḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite dvātriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 32//
2.32.d:
साधयामास निखिलं स्वकार्यं भृगुनन्दनः ।
निहत्य कार्त्तवीर्यं तं ससैन्यं सकुलं मुदा ।
विनिवृत्तो गृहं प्रागात्पितुः स्वस्य भृगूद्वहः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते द्वात्रिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 32॥
2.32.m:
The descendant of Bhṛgu accomplished his entire mission; / having joyfully slain Kārttavīrya along with his army and his clan, / the upholder of the Bhṛgu lineage returned and went to his father’s house.

Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, entitled ‘The Account of Bhārgava’, in the third Upoddhātapāda in the middle section of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

2.33.s:
sagara uvāca
śrutaṃ sarvaṃ muniśreṣṭha kīrtyamānaṃ tvayā vibho /
kavacaṃ vada sarvatra trailokyavijayapradam //
2.33.d:
सगर उवाच
श्रुतं सर्वं मुनिश्रेष्ठ कीर्त्यमानं त्वया विभो ।
कवचं वद सर्वत्र त्रैलोक्यविजयप्रदम् ॥
2.33.m: Sagara said: / Everything related by you, O best of sages, has been heard, O mighty one; / declare the armor that everywhere bestows victory over the three worlds.

2.33.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
śṛṇu vatsa pravakṣyāmi kavacaṃ paramādbhutam /
mantra ca siddhida śaśvatsādhakānāṃ sukhāvaham //
2.33.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
शृणु वत्स प्रवक्ष्यामि कवचं परमाद्भुतम् ।
मन्त्र च सिद्धिद शश्वत्साधकानां सुखावहम् ॥
2.33.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Listen, child, I shall declare the wondrous armor / and the mantra that constantly grants success and brings happiness to practitioners.

2.33.s:
gopījanapadasyāta vallabhāya samuccaret /
svāhānto 'yaṃ mahāmantro daśārṇo bhuktimuktidaḥ //
2.33.d:
गोपीजनपदस्यात वल्लभाय समुच्चरेत् ।
स्वाहान्तो ऽयं महामन्त्रो दशार्णो भुक्तिमुक्तिदः ॥
2.33.m: One should utter the word ‘gopījana’ and then ‘vallabhāya’; / ending in ‘svāhā’, this great ten-syllable mantra gives worldly enjoyment and liberation.

2.33.s:
sadāśivastvasya ṛṣiḥ paṅktiśchanda udāhṛtam /
devatā kṛṣṇa udito viniyogo 'khilāptaye //
2.33.d:
सदाशिवस्त्वस्य ऋषिः पङ्क्तिश्छन्द उदाहृतम् ।
देवता कृष्ण उदितो विनियोगो ऽखिलाप्तये ॥
2.33.m: Its sage is Sadāśiva, the meter is declared to be paṅkti, / the deity is proclaimed as Kṛṣṇa, and the ritual application is for the attainment of all ends.

2.33.s:
trailokyavijayasyātha kavacasya prajāpatiḥ /
ṛṣiśchandaśca jagatī devo rājeśvaraḥ svayam //
2.33.d:
त्रैलोक्यविजयस्याथ कवचस्य प्रजापतिः ।
ऋषिश्छन्दश्च जगती देवो राजेश्वरः स्वयम् ॥
2.33.m: Now of the Trailokyavijaya armor, Prajāpati is / the sage, the meter is jagatī, and the deity is Rājeśvara himself.

2.33.s:
trailokyavijayaprāptau viniyogaḥ prakīrttitaḥ /
praṇavo meśiraḥ pātu śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ sadā //
2.33.d:
त्रैलोक्यविजयप्राप्तौ विनियोगः प्रकीर्त्तितः ।
प्रणवो मेशिरः पातु श्रीकृष्णाय नमः सदा ॥
2.33.m: Its ritual application is declared to be for attaining victory over the three worlds: / May the Praṇava protect my head; always: ‘Homage to Śrī Kṛṣṇa!’

2.33.s:
pāyātkapālaṃ kṛṣṇāya svāheti satataṃ mama /
kṛṣṇeti pātu netre me kṛṣṇasvāheti tārakām //
2.33.d:
पायात्कपालं कृष्णाय स्वाहेति सततं मम ।
कृष्णेति पातु नेत्रे मे कृष्णस्वाहेति तारकाम् ॥
2.33.m: May ‘To Kṛṣṇa, svāhā!’ constantly protect my forehead; / may ‘Kṛṣṇa’ protect my two eyes; may ‘Kṛṣṇa, svāhā’ [protect] my pupil.

2.33.s:
haraye nama ityeṣa bhrūlatāṃ pātu me sadā /
oṃ govindāya svāheti nāsikāṃ pātu saṃtatam //
2.33.d:
हरये नम इत्येष भ्रूलतां पातु मे सदा ।
ओं गोविन्दाय स्वाहेति नासिकां पातु संततम् ॥
2.33.m: May ‘Homage to Hari!’ constantly protect my eyebrow; / may ‘Oṃ, to Govinda, svāhā!’ continuously protect my nose.

2.33.s:
gopālāya namo gaṇḍaṃ pātu me satataṃ manuḥ /
klīṃ kṛṣṇāya namaḥ karṇauṃ pātu kalpatarurmama //
2.33.d:
गोपालाय नमो गण्डं पातु मे सततं मनुः ।
क्लीं कृष्णाय नमः कर्णौं पातु कल्पतरुर्मम ॥
2.33.m: May the mantra ‘Homage to Gopāla!’ constantly protect my cheek; / may ‘Klīṃ, homage to Kṛṣṇa!’, the wish-granting tree, protect my ears.

2.33.s:
śrīṃ kṛṣṇāya namaḥ pātu nityaṃ me 'dharayugmakam /
oṃ gopīśāya svāheti dantapaṅktiṃ mamāvatu //
2.33.d:
श्रीं कृष्णाय नमः पातु नित्यं मे ऽधरयुग्मकम् ।
ओं गोपीशाय स्वाहेति दन्तपङ्क्तिं ममावतु ॥
2.33.m: May 'śrīṃ kṛṣṇāya namaḥ' protect my two lips forever; / may 'oṃ gopīśāya svāhā' guard my row of teeth.

2.33.s:
śrīkṛṣṇeti radacchidraṃ pātume tryakṣaro manuḥ /
oṃ śrīkṛṣṇāya svāheti jihvikāṃ pātu me sadā //
2.33.d:
श्रीकृष्णेति रदच्छिद्रं पातुमे त्र्यक्षरो मनुः ।
ओं श्रीकृष्णाय स्वाहेति जिह्विकां पातु मे सदा ॥
2.33.m: May the three-syllable mantra 'śrīkṛṣṇa' protect my mouth; / may 'oṃ śrīkṛṣṇāya svāhā' always protect my tongue.

2.33.s:
rāmeśvarāya svāheti tālukaṃ pātu me sadā /
rādhikeśāya svāheti kaṇṭhaṃ me pātu sarvadā //
2.33.d:
रामेश्वराय स्वाहेति तालुकं पातु मे सदा ।
राधिकेशाय स्वाहेति कण्ठं मे पातु सर्वदा ॥
2.33.m: May 'rāmeśvarāya svāhā' always protect my palate; / may 'rādhikeśāya svāhā' always protect my throat.

2.33.s:
namo gopīgaṇeśāya grīvāṃ me pātu sarvadā /
oṃ gopeśāya svāheti skandhau pātu sadā mama //
2.33.d:
नमो गोपीगणेशाय ग्रीवां मे पातु सर्वदा ।
ओं गोपेशाय स्वाहेति स्कन्धौ पातु सदा मम ॥
2.33.m: May 'namo gopīgaṇeśāya' always protect my neck; / may 'oṃ gopeśāya svāhā' always protect my shoulders.

2.33.s:
namaḥ kiśoraveṣāya svāhā pṛṣṭhaṃ mamāvatu /
udaraṃ pātu me nityaṃ mukundāya namo manuḥ //
2.33.d:
नमः किशोरवेषाय स्वाहा पृष्ठं ममावतु ।
उदरं पातु मे नित्यं मुकुन्दाय नमो मनुः ॥
2.33.m: May 'namaḥ kiśoraveṣāya svāhā' guard my back; / may the mantra 'mukundāya namaḥ' constantly protect my belly.

2.33.s:
hnīṃ śrīṅklīṅkṛṣṇāya svāhā karau pātu sadā mama /
oṃ viṣṇave namaḥ svāhā bāhuyugmaṃ mamāvatu //
2.33.d:
ह्नीं श्रीङ्क्लीङ्कृष्णाय स्वाहा करौ पातु सदा मम ।
ओं विष्णवे नमः स्वाहा बाहुयुग्मं ममावतु ॥
2.33.m: May 'hnīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ kṛṣṇāya svāhā' always protect my hands; / may 'oṃ viṣṇave namaḥ svāhā' guard my pair of arms.

2.33.s:
oṃ hrīṃbhagavate svāhā nakhapaṅktiṃ mamāvatu /
namo nārāyaṇāyeti nakharandhraṃ mamāvatu //
2.33.d:
ओं ह्रींभगवते स्वाहा नखपङ्क्तिं ममावतु ।
नमो नारायणायेति नखरन्ध्रं ममावतु ॥
2.33.m: May 'oṃ hrīṃ bhagavate svāhā' guard my rows of nails; / may 'namo nārāyaṇāya' guard the hollows beneath my nails.

2.33.s:
oṃ hrīṃśrīṃpadmanābhāya nābhiṃ pātu sadā mama /
oṃ sarveśāya svāheti keśānmama sadāvatu //
2.33.d:
ओं ह्रींश्रींपद्मनाभाय नाभिं पातु सदा मम ।
ओं सर्वेशाय स्वाहेति केशान्मम सदावतु ॥
2.33.m: May 'oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ padmanābhāya' always protect my navel; / may 'oṃ sarveśāya svāhā' always guard my hair.

2.33.s:
namaḥ kṛṣṇāya svāheti brahmarandhraṃ sadāvatu /
oṃ mādhavāya svāheti bhālaṃ me sarvadāvatu //
2.33.d:
नमः कृष्णाय स्वाहेति ब्रह्मरन्ध्रं सदावतु ।
ओं माधवाय स्वाहेति भालं मे सर्वदावतु ॥
2.33.m: May 'namaḥ kṛṣṇāya svāhā' always guard my brahmarandhra; / may 'oṃ mādhavāya svāhā' always guard my forehead.

2.33.s:
oṃ hrīṃśrīṃrasikeśāya kaṭiṃ mama sadāvatu /
namo gopījaneśāya ūrū pātu sadā mama //
2.33.d:
ओं ह्रींश्रींरसिकेशाय कटिं मम सदावतु ।
नमो गोपीजनेशाय ऊरू पातु सदा मम ॥
2.33.m: May 'oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rasikeśāya' always guard my waist; / may 'namo gopījaneśāya' always protect my thighs.

2.33.s:
oṃ namo daityanāśāya svāhetyavatu jānunī /
yaśodānandanāyeti namoto jaṅghake 'vatu //
2.33.d:
ओं नमो दैत्यनाशाय स्वाहेत्यवतु जानुनी ।
यशोदानन्दनायेति नमोतो जङ्घके ऽवतु ॥
2.33.m: May 'oṃ namo daityanāśāya svāhā' guard my knees; / ending with 'namas', may 'yaśodānandanāya' guard my shanks.

2.33.s:
rāsāraṃbhapriyāyeti svāhānto hīṃ mamāvatu /
vṛndāpriyāya svāheti sakalāṅgāni me 'vatu //
2.33.d:
रासारंभप्रियायेति स्वाहान्तो हीं ममावतु ।
वृन्दाप्रियाय स्वाहेति सकलाङ्गानि मे ऽवतु ॥
2.33.m: May 'rāsāraṃbhapriyāya' ending in 'svāhā', [preceded by] 'hrīṃ', guard me; / may 'vṛndāpriyāya svāhā' guard all my limbs.

2.33.s:
pariburṇamanāḥ kṛṣmaḥ prācyāṃ māṃ sarvadāvatu /
svayaṃ golokanātho māmāgneyyāṃ diśi rakṣatu //
2.33.d:
परिबुर्णमनाः कृष्मः प्राच्यां मां सर्वदावतु ।
स्वयं गोलोकनाथो मामाग्नेय्यां दिशि रक्षतु ॥
2.33.m: May Kṛṣṇa, whose mind is fulfilled, always protect me in the east; / may the Lord of Goloka himself protect me in the southeast.

2.33.s:
pūrṇabrahmasvarūpaśca dakṣiṇe māṃ sadāvatu /
nairṛtyāṃ pātu māṃ kṛṣṇāḥ paścime pātu māṃ hariḥ //
2.33.d:
पूर्णब्रह्मस्वरूपश्च दक्षिणे मां सदावतु ।
नैरृत्यां पातु मां कृष्णाः पश्चिमे पातु मां हरिः ॥
2.33.m: May he whose nature is the full Brahman always protect me in the south; / may Kṛṣṇa protect me in the southwest; may Hari protect me in the west.

2.33.s:
govindaḥ pātu vāyavyāmuttare rasikeśvaraḥ /
aiśānyāṃ me sadā pātu vṛndāvanavihāra kṛt //
2.33.d:
गोविन्दः पातु वायव्यामुत्तरे रसिकेश्वरः ।
ऐशान्यां मे सदा पातु वृन्दावनविहार कृत् ॥
2.33.m: May Govinda protect me in the northwest, and in the north the Lord of the impassioned; / may the one who disports in Vṛndāvana always protect me in the northeast.

2.33.s:
vṛndāprāṇeśvaraḥ śaśvatpātu māmūrddhvadeśataḥ /
sadaiva māmadhaḥ pātu balidhvaṃsī mahābalaḥ //
2.33.d:
वृन्दाप्राणेश्वरः शश्वत्पातु मामूर्द्ध्वदेशतः ।
सदैव मामधः पातु बलिध्वंसी महाबलः ॥
2.33.m: May the lord of Vṛndā's life continually protect me from above; / may the mighty crusher of Bali always protect me from below.

2.33.s:
jale sthale cāntarikṣe nṛsiṃhaḥ pātu māṃ sadā /
svapne jāgaraṇe caiva pātu māṃ mādhavaḥ svayam //
2.33.d:
जले स्थले चान्तरिक्षे नृसिंहः पातु मां सदा ।
स्वप्ने जागरणे चैव पातु मां माधवः स्वयम् ॥
2.33.m: In water, on land, and in the sky, may Nṛsiṃha always protect me; / in dreaming and in waking, may Mādhava himself protect me.

2.33.s:
sarvāntarātmā nirliptaḥ pātu māṃ sarvato vibhuḥ /
iti te kathitaṃ bhūpa sarvāghaughavināśanam //
2.33.d:
सर्वान्तरात्मा निर्लिप्तः पातु मां सर्वतो विभुः ।
इति ते कथितं भूप सर्वाघौघविनाशनम् ॥
2.33.m: May the all-pervading Inner Self of all, free from attachment, protect me on every side. / Thus has been told to you, O king, that which destroys the multitude of all sins,

2.33.s:
trailokyavijayaṃ nāma kavacaṃ parameśituḥ /
mayā śrutaṃ śivamukhātpravaktavyaṃ na kasyacit //
2.33.d:
त्रैलोक्यविजयं नाम कवचं परमेशितुः ।
मया श्रुतं शिवमुखात्प्रवक्तव्यं न कस्यचित् ॥
2.33.m: the armour of the Supreme Lord named Trailokyavijaya ('Conquest of the Three Worlds'). / It was heard by me from the mouth of Śiva, and must not be spoken to anyone.

2.33.s:
gurumabhyarcya vidhivatkavacaṃ dhārayettu yaḥ /
kaṇṭhe vā dakṣiṇe bāhau so 'pi viṣṇurna saṃśayaḥ //
2.33.d:
गुरुमभ्यर्च्य विधिवत्कवचं धारयेत्तु यः ।
कण्ठे वा दक्षिणे बाहौ सो ऽपि विष्णुर्न संशयः ॥
2.33.m: Whoever, having properly worshipped his guru, wears this armour / around his neck or on his right arm, he too is Viṣṇu, without doubt.

2.33.s:
sa sādhako 'vasadyatra tatra vāṇīrame sthite /
yadi syātsiddhakavaco jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ //
2.33.d:
स साधको ऽवसद्यत्र तत्र वाणीरमे स्थिते ।
यदि स्यात्सिद्धकवचो जीवन्मुक्तो न संशयः ॥
2.33.m: Wherever that practitioner dwells, Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī abide there. / If he has mastered the armour, he is liberated while living, without doubt.

2.33.s:
niścitaṃ koṭivarṣāṇāṃ pūjāyāḥ phalamāpnuyāt /
rājasūryasahasrāṇi vājapeyaśatāni ca //
2.33.d:
निश्चितं कोटिवर्षाणां पूजायाः फलमाप्नुयात् ।
राजसूर्यसहस्राणि वाजपेयशतानि च ॥
2.33.m: He surely attains the fruit of ten million years of worship; / thousands of royal consecrations (rājasūya) and hundreds of vājapeya sacrifices,

2.33.s:
mahādānāni yānyeva bhuvaścāpi pradakṣiṇā /
trailokyavijayasyāsya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm //
2.33.d:
महादानानि यान्येव भुवश्चापि प्रदक्षिणा ।
त्रैलोक्यविजयस्यास्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् ॥
2.33.m: whatever great gifts there be, and circumambulating the earth— / they are not worth a sixteenth part of this Trailokyavijaya [armour].

2.33.s:
vratopavāsaniyamāḥ svādhyāyādhyayane tathā /
snānaṃ ca sarvatīrtheṣu nāsyārhanti kalāmapi //
2.33.d:
व्रतोपवासनियमाः स्वाध्यायाध्ययने तथा ।
स्नानं च सर्वतीर्थेषु नास्यार्हन्ति कलामपि ॥
2.33.m: Vows, fasts, observances, recitation and study of the Veda, / and bathing at all sacred places are not worth even a fraction of this.

2.33.s:
siddhatvamamaratvaṃ ca dāsatvaṃ śrīharerapi /
yadi syātsiddhakavacaḥ sarvaṃ prāpnoti niścitam //
2.33.d:
सिद्धत्वममरत्वं च दासत्वं श्रीहरेरपि ।
यदि स्यात्सिद्धकवचः सर्वं प्राप्नोति निश्चितम् ॥
2.33.m: Attainment of perfections, immortality, and servitude to glorious Hari— / if one has mastered the armour, one surely obtains all this.

2.33.s:
sa bhavetsiddhakavaco daśalakṣaṃ japettu yaḥ /
yo bhavetsiddhakavaco vijayī sa bhaved dhruvam //
2.33.d:
स भवेत्सिद्धकवचो दशलक्षं जपेत्तु यः ।
यो भवेत्सिद्धकवचो विजयी स भवेद् ध्रुवम् ॥
2.33.m: He who recites [it] a million times becomes one who has mastered the armour; / whoever becomes one who has mastered the armour is certainly victorious.

2.33.s:
rājyaṃ deyaṃ śiro deyaṃ prāṇā deyāśca bhūpate /
etattu kavacaṃ vatsa na deyaṃ saṃkaṭe 'pi ca //
2.33.d:
राज्यं देयं शिरो देयं प्राणा देयाश्च भूपते ।
एतत्तु कवचं वत्स न देयं संकटे ऽपि च ॥
2.33.m: A kingdom may be given away, one's head may be given away, and one's life may be given away, O king; / but this armour, dear child, must not be given away, even in extremity.

2.33.s:
mayā prakāśitaṃ yatte caiteṣāṃ trāṇakāraṇāt /
mamājñākaraṇāccaiva tadviddhi kulabhāskara /
idaṃ dhṛtvā tu kavacaṃ cakravarttī bhavānbhava //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite trayastriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.33.d:
मया प्रकाशितं यत्ते चैतेषां त्राणकारणात् ।
ममाज्ञाकरणाच्चैव तद्विद्धि कुलभास्कर ।
इदं धृत्वा तु कवचं चक्रवर्त्ती भवान्भव ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते त्रयस्त्रिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.33.m:
Know, O sun of your lineage, that it has been revealed to you by me for the sake of protecting these people / and because you obey my command; / having put on this armour, become a universal monarch!

Thus ends the thirty-third chapter in the deeds of Bhārgava, in the third Upoddhātapāda in the middle section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

2.34.s:
sagara uvāca
brahmaputra mahābhāga mahānme 'nugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ /
yadidaṃ kavacaṃ mahyaṃ prakāśitamanāmayam //
2.34.d:
सगर उवाच
ब्रह्मपुत्र महाभाग महान्मे ऽनुग्रहः कृतः ।
यदिदं कवचं मह्यं प्रकाशितमनामयम् ॥
2.34.m: Sagara said: / O fortunate son of Brahmā, a great favor has been done to me, / in that this auspicious armour has been revealed to me.

2.34.s:
aurveṇānugṛhīto 'haṃ kṛtāstro yadanugrahāt /
bhavatastu kṛpāpātraṃ jāto 'hamadhunā vibho //
2.34.d:
और्वेणानुगृहीतो ऽहं कृतास्त्रो यदनुग्रहात् ।
भवतस्तु कृपापात्रं जातो ऽहमधुना विभो ॥
2.34.m: I was favoured by Aurva, by whose grace I mastered weapons; / and now, O lord, I have become the recipient of your grace.

2.34.s:
rāmeṇa bhārgavendreṇa kārttavīryo nṛpo guro /
yathā samāpito vīrastanme vistarato vada //
2.34.d:
रामेण भार्गवेन्द्रेण कार्त्तवीर्यो नृपो गुरो ।
यथा समापितो वीरस्तन्मे विस्तरतो वद ॥
2.34.m: How King Kārttavīrya, that hero, was slain by Rāma, / the foremost of the Bhārgavas, O guru—tell me that in detail.

2.34.s:
kṛpāpātraṃ sa dattasya rājā rāmaḥ śivasya ca /
ubhau tau samare vīrau jaghaṭāte kathaṃ guro //
2.34.d:
कृपापात्रं स दत्तस्य राजा रामः शिवस्य च ।
उभौ तौ समरे वीरौ जघटाते कथं गुरो ॥
2.34.m: That king was the object of Datta's grace, and Rāma of Śiva's; / how did those two heroes clash in battle, O guru?

2.34.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
śṛṇu rājanpravakṣyāmi caritaṃ pāpanāśanam /
kārttavīryasya bhūpasya rāmasya ca mahātmanaḥ //
2.34.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
शृणु राजन्प्रवक्ष्यामि चरितं पापनाशनम् ।
कार्त्तवीर्यस्य भूपस्य रामस्य च महात्मनः ॥
2.34.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Listen, O king, and I shall tell the sin-destroying story / of King Kārttavīrya and of the great-souled Rāma.

2.34.s:
sa rāmaḥ kavacaṃ labdhvā mantraṃ caiva gurormukhāt /
cakāra mādhanaṃ tasya bhaktyā paramayā yutaḥ //
2.34.d:
स रामः कवचं लब्ध्वा मन्त्रं चैव गुरोर्मुखात् ।
चकार माधनं तस्य भक्त्या परमया युतः ॥
2.34.m: Having obtained the armour and the mantra from the mouth of his guru, / that Rāma practiced its propitiation, endowed with supreme devotion.

2.34.s:
bhūmiśāgī triṣavaṇa snānasadhyāparāyaṇaḥ /
uvāsapuṣkare rāma śatavarṣamatandritaḥ //
2.34.d:
भूमिशागी त्रिषवण स्नानसध्यापरायणः ।
उवासपुष्करे राम शतवर्षमतन्द्रितः ॥
2.34.m: Sleeping on the ground, devoted to the three daily ablutions and twilight prayers, / Rāma lived at Puṣkara for a hundred years, unwearied.

2.34.s:
samitpuṣpakuśādīni dravyāṇyaharaharbhṛgoḥ /
ānīya kānanādbhūpa prāyacchadakṛtavraṇaḥ //
2.34.d:
समित्पुष्पकुशादीनि द्रव्याण्यहरहर्भृगोः ।
आनीय काननाद्भूप प्रायच्छदकृतव्रणः ॥
2.34.m: Fetching items such as firewood, flowers, and kuśa grass from the forest day after day, / Akṛtavraṇa gave them to the descendant of Bhṛgu, O king.

2.34.s:
satataṃ dhyānasaṃyukto rāmo matimatāṃ varaḥ /
ārādhayāmāsa vibhuṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kalmaṣanāśanam //
2.34.d:
सततं ध्यानसंयुक्तो रामो मतिमतां वरः ।
आराधयामास विभुं कृष्णं कल्मषनाशनम् ॥
2.34.m: Always engaged in meditation, Rāma, best among the wise, / worshipped the all-pervading Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of blemishes.

2.34.s:
tasyaivaṃ yajamānasya rāmasya jagatīpate /
gataṃ varṣaśataṃ tatra dhyānayuktasya nityadā //
2.34.d:
तस्यैवं यजमानस्य रामस्य जगतीपते ।
गतं वर्षशतं तत्र ध्यानयुक्तस्य नित्यदा ॥
2.34.m: As Rāma was worshipping thus, O lord of the earth, / a hundred years passed there while he was constantly engaged in meditation.

2.34.s:
ekadā tu mahārāja rāmaḥ snātuṃ gato mahān /
madhyamaṃ puṣkaraṃ tatra dadarśāśvaryamuttamam //
2.34.d:
एकदा तु महाराज रामः स्नातुं गतो महान् ।
मध्यमं पुष्करं तत्र ददर्शाश्वर्यमुत्तमम् ॥
2.34.m: Once, O great king, when the great Rāma went to bathe / at middle Puṣkara, he saw a supreme wonder there.

2.34.s:
mṛga ekaḥ samāyāto mṛgya yuktaḥ palāyitaḥ /
vyādhasya mṛgayāṃ prāpto dharmatapto 'tipīḍitaḥ //
2.34.d:
मृग एकः समायातो मृग्य युक्तः पलायितः ।
व्याधस्य मृगयां प्राप्तो धर्मतप्तो ऽतिपीडितः ॥
2.34.m: A stag arrived, fleeing along with a hind, / having been caught in a hunter's hunt, scorched by the heat, deeply distressed,

2.34.s:
pipāsito mahābhāga jalapānasamutsukaḥ /
rāmasya paśyatastatra sarasastaṭamāgataḥ //
2.34.d:
पिपासितो महाभाग जलपानसमुत्सुकः ।
रामस्य पश्यतस्तत्र सरसस्तटमागतः ॥
2.34.m: thirsty, O fortunate one, and eager to drink water. / As Rāma watched, he came to the bank of the lake there.

2.34.s:
paścānmṛgī samāyātā bhītā sā cakitekṣaṇā /
ubho tau pibatastatra jalaṃ śaṅkitamānasau //
2.34.d:
पश्चान्मृगी समायाता भीता सा चकितेक्षणा ।
उभो तौ पिबतस्तत्र जलं शङ्कितमानसौ ॥
2.34.m: Behind him came the hind, frightened, her eyes startled; / both drank water there, their minds apprehensive.

2.34.s:
tāvatsamāgato vyādho bāṇapāṇirdhanurddharaḥ /
sa dṛṣṭvā tatra saṃviṣṭaṃ rāmaṃ bhārgavanandanam //
2.34.d:
तावत्समागतो व्याधो बाणपाणिर्धनुर्द्धरः ।
स दृष्ट्वा तत्र संविष्टं रामं भार्गवनन्दनम् ॥
2.34.m: Just then the hunter arrived, arrow in hand, holding a bow; / seeing Rāma, the delight of the Bhārgavas, seated there,

2.34.s:
akṛtavraṇasaṃyuktaṃ tasthau dūrakṛtekṣaṇaḥ /
sa cintayāmāsa tadā śaṅkito bhṛgunandanāt //
2.34.d:
अकृतव्रणसंयुक्तं तस्थौ दूरकृतेक्षणः ।
स चिन्तयामास तदा शङ्कितो भृगुनन्दनात् ॥
2.34.m: accompanied by Akṛtavraṇa, he halted, casting his gaze from afar; / he then reflected, apprehensive of the descendant of Bhṛgu:

2.34.s:
ayaṃ rāmo mahāvīro duṣṭānāmantakārakaḥ /
kathametasya hanmyetau paśyato mṛgayāmṛgau //
2.34.d:
अयं रामो महावीरो दुष्टानामन्तकारकः ।
कथमेतस्य हन्म्येतौ पश्यतो मृगयामृगौ ॥
2.34.m: 'This Rāma is a great hero, the destroyer of the wicked; / how can I kill these two hunted deer while he is watching?'

2.34.s:
iti cintā samāviṣṭo vyādho rājanyasattama /
tasthau tatraiva rāmasya bhayātsaṃtrastamānasaḥ //
2.34.d:
इति चिन्ता समाविष्टो व्याधो राजन्यसत्तम ।
तस्थौ तत्रैव रामस्य भयात्संत्रस्तमानसः ॥
2.34.m: Absorbed in such anxiety, O best of kings, / the hunter stayed right there, his mind terrified out of fear of Rāma.

2.34.s:
rāmastu tau mṛgoṃ dṛṣṭvā pibantau sabhyaṃ jalam /
tarkayāmāsa medhāvī kimatra bhayakāraṇam //
2.34.d:
रामस्तु तौ मृगों दृष्ट्वा पिबन्तौ सभ्यं जलम् ।
तर्कयामास मेधावी किमत्र भयकारणम् ॥
2.34.m: Rāma, seeing those two deer drinking water fearlessly, / and being wise, reflected: 'What is the cause of fear here?'

2.34.s:
naivātra vyāghrasenādo na ca vyādho hi dṛśyate /
kenaitau kāraṇenāho śaṅkitau cakitekṣaṇau //
2.34.d:
नैवात्र व्याघ्रसेनादो न च व्याधो हि दृश्यते ।
केनैतौ कारणेनाहो शङ्कितौ चकितेक्षणौ ॥
2.34.m: "Indeed, neither the sound of a tiger nor a hunter is seen here; / for what reason, then, are these two suspicious, with startled eyes?

2.34.s:
atha vā mṛgajātirhi nisargāccakitekṣaṇā /
cenaitau jalapāne 'pi paśyataścakitekṣaṇau //
2.34.d:
अथ वा मृगजातिर्हि निसर्गाच्चकितेक्षणा ।
चेनैतौ जलपाने ऽपि पश्यतश्चकितेक्षणौ ॥
2.34.m: Or is the species of deer by nature possessed of startled eyes, / since, even while drinking water, they look about with frightened gaze?

2.34.s:
naitāvatkāraṇaṃ cātra kintu khedabhayāturau /
lakṣayete khinnasarvāṅgau kampayuktau yatastvimau //
2.34.d:
नैतावत्कारणं चात्र किन्तु खेदभयातुरौ ।
लक्षयेते खिन्नसर्वाङ्गौ कम्पयुक्तौ यतस्त्विमौ ॥
2.34.m: Yet this is not the only reason here; rather, they are afflicted by exhaustion and fear, / since they appear with their whole bodies weary and trembling."

2.34.s:
evaṃ saṃcintya matimānsa tasthau madhyapuṣkare /
śiṣyeṇa saṃyuto rāmo yāvattau cāpi saṃsthitau //
2.34.d:
एवं संचिन्त्य मतिमान्स तस्थौ मध्यपुष्करे ।
शिष्येण संयुतो रामो यावत्तौ चापि संस्थितौ ॥
2.34.m: Having reflected thus, the wise Rāma remained in the middle lake / together with his disciple, as long as those two remained.

2.34.s:
pītvā jalaṃ tatastau tu vṛkṣacchāyāsamāśritau /
rāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātmānaṃ kathāṃ tau cakraturmudā //
2.34.d:
पीत्वा जलं ततस्तौ तु वृक्षच्छायासमाश्रितौ ।
रामं दृष्ट्वा महात्मानं कथां तौ चक्रतुर्मुदा ॥
2.34.m: Having drunk the water, the two took shelter in the shade of a tree; / seeing the great-souled Rāma, they gladly conversed.

2.34.s:
mṛgyuvāca
kānta cātraiva tiṣṭhāvo yāvadrāmo 'trasaṃsthitaḥ /
asya vīrasya sāṃnidhye bhayaṃ naivāvayorbhavet //
2.34.d:
मृग्युवाच
कान्त चात्रैव तिष्ठावो यावद्रामो ऽत्रसंस्थितः ।
अस्य वीरस्य सांनिध्ये भयं नैवावयोर्भवेत् ॥
2.34.m:
The doe said:
"Beloved, let us stay right here as long as Rāma remains here; / in the presence of this hero, no fear can come to the two of us.

2.34.s:
atrāpyāgatya caivdyādhau hyāvayoḥ prahariṣyati /
dṛṣṭamātro hi muninā bhasmībhūto bhaviṣyati //
2.34.d:
अत्राप्यागत्य चैव्द्याधौ ह्यावयोः प्रहरिष्यति ।
दृष्टमात्रो हि मुनिना भस्मीभूतो भविष्यति ॥
2.34.m: Even if the hunter comes here and strikes at the two of us, / as soon as he is seen by the sage, he will be reduced to ashes."

2.34.s:
ityukte vacane mṛgyā rāmar śanatuṣṭayā /
mṛgaścovāca harṣeṇa samāviṣṭaḥ priyāṃ svakām //
2.34.d:
इत्युक्ते वचने मृग्या रामर् शनतुष्टया ।
मृगश्चोवाच हर्षेण समाविष्टः प्रियां स्वकाम् ॥
2.34.m: When this statement was made by the doe, pleased at the sight of Rāma, / the buck, filled with joy, spoke to his beloved:

2.34.s:
evameva mahābhāge yadvai vadasi bhāmini /
jāne 'hamapi rāmasya prabhāvaṃ sumahātmanaḥ //
2.34.d:
एवमेव महाभागे यद्वै वदसि भामिनि ।
जाने ऽहमपि रामस्य प्रभावं सुमहात्मनः ॥
2.34.m: "Just so, illustrious lady, what you say is true, beautiful one; / I too know the power of this very great-souled Rāma.

2.34.s:
yo 'yaṃ saṃdṛśyate cāsya pārśvaṃ śiṣyo 'kṛtavraṇaḥ /
sacāne na mahābhāgastrāto vyāghrabhayāturaḥ //
2.34.d:
यो ऽयं संदृश्यते चास्य पार्श्वं शिष्यो ऽकृतव्रणः ।
सचाने न महाभागस्त्रातो व्याघ्रभयातुरः ॥
2.34.m: This disciple of his, Akṛtavraṇa, who is seen at his side, / this illustrious one was rescued by him when afflicted by fear of a tiger.

2.34.s:
ayaṃ rāmo mahābhāge jamadagnisuto 'nujaḥ /
pitaraṃ kārttavīryeṇa dṛṣṭvā caiva tiraskṛtam //
2.34.d:
अयं रामो महाभागे जमदग्निसुतो ऽनुजः ।
पितरं कार्त्तवीर्येण दृष्ट्वा चैव तिरस्कृतम् ॥
2.34.m: This Rāma, O fortunate one, is the younger son of Jamadagni; / seeing his father insulted by Kārttavīrya,

2.34.s:
cakārātitarāṃ kruddhaḥ pratijñāṃ nṛpaghātinīm /
tatpūrtikāmo hyagamadbrahmalokaṃ purā hyayam //
2.34.d:
चकारातितरां क्रुद्धः प्रतिज्ञां नृपघातिनीम् ।
तत्पूर्तिकामो ह्यगमद्ब्रह्मलोकं पुरा ह्ययम् ॥
2.34.m: he, exceedingly enraged, made a vow to slay the kings; / wishing to fulfill that, he formerly went to the world of Brahmā.

2.34.s:
sa brahmā diṣṭavāṃścainaṃ śivalokaṃ vrajeti ha /
tasya tvājñāṃ samādāya gato 'sau śivasannidhim //
2.34.d:
स ब्रह्मा दिष्टवांश्चैनं शिवलोकं व्रजेति ह ।
तस्य त्वाज्ञां समादाय गतो ऽसौ शिवसन्निधिम् ॥
2.34.m: That Brahmā instructed him: 'Go to the world of Śiva.' / Receiving his command, he went into the presence of Śiva.

2.34.s:
provācākhilavṛttānta rājñaścapyātmanaḥ pituḥ /
sa kṛpālurmahādevaḥ sabhājya bhṛgunandanam //
2.34.d:
प्रोवाचाखिलवृत्तान्त राज्ञश्चप्यात्मनः पितुः ।
स कृपालुर्महादेवः सभाज्य भृगुनन्दनम् ॥
2.34.m: He told the entire story of the king and of his own father; / compassionate Mahādeva, honoring the descendant of Bhṛgu,

2.34.s:
dadau kṛṣṇasya sanmantramabhedyaṃ kavacaṃ tathā /
svīyaṃ pāśupataṃ cāstramanyāstragrāmameva ca //
2.34.d:
ददौ कृष्णस्य सन्मन्त्रमभेद्यं कवचं तथा ।
स्वीयं पाशुपतं चास्त्रमन्यास्त्रग्राममेव च ॥
2.34.m: gave him the excellent mantra of Kṛṣṇa and an impenetrable armor, / as well as his own Pāśupata missile and an entire host of other missiles.

2.34.s:
visarjayāmāsa mudā dattvā śastrāṇi cādarāt /
so 'yamatrāgato bhadre metrasādhanatatparaḥ //
2.34.d:
विसर्जयामास मुदा दत्त्वा शस्त्राणि चादरात् ।
सो ऽयमत्रागतो भद्रे मेत्रसाधनतत्परः ॥
2.34.m: Having respectfully given him the weapons, he dismissed him with joy; / this very one has come here, gentle lady, intent upon accomplishing the mantra.

2.34.s:
nityaṃ japati dharmātmā kṛṣṇasya kavacaṃ sudhīḥ /
śatavarṣāṇi cāpyasya gatāni sumahātmanaḥ //
2.34.d:
नित्यं जपति धर्मात्मा कृष्णस्य कवचं सुधीः ।
शतवर्षाणि चाप्यस्य गतानि सुमहात्मनः ॥
2.34.m: The righteous, wise one constantly repeats the armor of Kṛṣṇa; / a hundred years have passed for this very great-souled one

2.34.s:
mantra sādhayato bhadre na ca tatsiddhireti hi /
ātrāsti kāraṇaṃ bhaktiḥ sāva vai trividhā matā //
2.34.d:
मन्त्र साधयतो भद्रे न च तत्सिद्धिरेति हि ।
आत्रास्ति कारणं भक्तिः साव वै त्रिविधा मता ॥
2.34.m: as he accomplishes the mantra, gentle lady, yet success does not come to it; / here devotion is the cause, and that [devotion] is considered to be threefold,

2.34.s:
uttamā madhyamā caiva kaniṣṭhā taralekṣaṇe /
śivasya nāradasyāpi śukasya ca mahātmanaḥ //
2.34.d:
उत्तमा मध्यमा चैव कनिष्ठा तरलेक्षणे ।
शिवस्य नारदस्यापि शुकस्य च महात्मनः ॥
2.34.m: highest, intermediate, and lowest, O restless-eyed lady! / Śiva, Nārada, and the great-souled Śuka,

2.34.s:
aṃbarīṣsya rājarṣe rantidevasya māruteḥ /
balervibhīṣaṇasyāpi prahlādasya mahātmanaḥ //
2.34.d:
अंबरीष्स्य राजर्षे रन्तिदेवस्य मारुतेः ।
बलेर्विभीषणस्यापि प्रह्लादस्य महात्मनः ॥
2.34.m: the royal sage Ambarīṣa, Rantideva, the son of the Wind, / Bali, Vibhīṣaṇa, and the great-souled Prahlāda,

2.34.s:
uttamā bhaktirevāsti gopīnāmuddhavasya ca /
vasiṣṭhādimunīśānāṃ manvādīnāṃ śubhekṣaṇe //
2.34.d:
उत्तमा भक्तिरेवास्ति गोपीनामुद्धवस्य च ।
वसिष्ठादिमुनीशानां मन्वादीनां शुभेक्षणे ॥
2.34.m: the gopīs, and Uddhava possess highest devotion; / of the lords of sages beginning with Vasiṣṭha, and Manu and others, O fair-eyed one,

2.34.s:
madhyā ca bhaktirevāsti prākṛtānyajaneṣu sā /
madhyabhaktirayaṃ rāmo nityaṃ yamaparāyaṇaḥ //
2.34.d:
मध्या च भक्तिरेवास्ति प्राकृतान्यजनेषु सा ।
मध्यभक्तिरयं रामो नित्यं यमपरायणः ॥
2.34.m: there is intermediate devotion; and that [lowest devotion] is found among ordinary people; / having intermediate devotion, this Rāma, ever devoted to self-restraint,

2.34.s:
sevate gopikādhīśaṃ tena siddhiṃ na cāgataḥ /
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityuktā tvaritaṃ kāntaṃ sā mṛgī hṛṣṭamānasā //
2.34.d:
सेवते गोपिकाधीशं तेन सिद्धिं न चागतः ।
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्युक्ता त्वरितं कान्तं सा मृगी हृष्टमानसा ॥
2.34.m:
serves the Lord of the cowherdesses, and therefore he has not attained accomplishment."
Vasiṣṭha said:
Thus spoken to, that doe, delighted in mind, swiftly

2.34.s:
punaḥ papraccha bhaktestu lakṣaṇaṃ premadāyakam /
mṛgyuvāca
sādhukānta mahābhāga vacaste 'laukikaṃ priya /
rhadṛg jñānaṃ tava kathaṃ saṃjātaṃ tadvadādhunā //
2.34.d:
पुनः पप्रच्छ भक्तेस्तु लक्षणं प्रेमदायकम् ।
मृग्युवाच
साधुकान्त महाभाग वचस्ते ऽलौकिकं प्रिय ।
र्हदृग् ज्ञानं तव कथं संजातं तद्वदाधुना ॥
2.34.m:
asked her beloved again about the characteristics of devotion that bestows love.
The doe said:
"Well said, my beloved, illustrious one, your word is extraordinary, dear one! / How has such knowledge arisen in you? Tell that now."

2.34.s:
mṛga uvāca
śṛṇu priye mahābhāge jñānaṃ puṇyena jāyate //
2.34.d:
मृग उवाच
शृणु प्रिये महाभागे ज्ञानं पुण्येन जायते ॥
2.34.m:
The buck said:
"Listen, my beloved, illustrious lady: knowledge arises through merit.

2.34.s:
tatpuṇyamadya saṃjātaṃ bhārgavasyāsya darśanāt /
puṇyātmā bhārgavaścāyaṃ kṛṣṇābhakto jitendriyaḥ //
2.34.d:
तत्पुण्यमद्य संजातं भार्गवस्यास्य दर्शनात् ।
पुण्यात्मा भार्गवश्चायं कृष्णाभक्तो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
2.34.m: That merit has arisen today from the sight of this Bhārgava; / this Bhārgava is a virtuous soul, devoted to Kṛṣṇa, with senses conquered,

2.34.s:
guruśuśrūṣako nityaṃ nityanaimittikādaraḥ /
ato 'sya darśanājjātaṃ jñānaṃ me/dyaiva bhāmini //
2.34.d:
गुरुशुश्रूषको नित्यं नित्यनैमित्तिकादरः ।
अतो ऽस्य दर्शनाज्जातं ज्ञानं मे।द्यैव भामिनि ॥
2.34.m: ever serving his guru, attentive to obligatory and occasional rites; / therefore, from the sight of him, knowledge has arisen in me this very day, beautiful lady,

2.34.s:
trailokyasthitasattvānāṃ śubhāśubhanidarśakam /
adyaiva viditaṃ me 'bhūdrāsasyāsya mahātmanaḥ //
2.34.d:
त्रैलोक्यस्थितसत्त्वानां शुभाशुभनिदर्शकम् ।
अद्यैव विदितं मे ऽभूद्रासस्यास्य महात्मनः ॥
2.34.m: which shows the good and evil of living beings in the three worlds; / this very day the deed of this great-souled Rāma has become known to me,

2.34.s:
caritaṃ puṇyadaṃ caiva pāpaghnaṃ śṛṇvatāmidam /
yadyatkariṣyate caiva tadapi jñānagocaram //
2.34.d:
चरितं पुण्यदं चैव पापघ्नं शृण्वतामिदम् ।
यद्यत्करिष्यते चैव तदपि ज्ञानगोचरम् ॥
2.34.m: which bestows merit and destroys sin for those who hear it; / and whatever he will do is also within the range of my knowledge.

2.34.s:
yottamā bhaktirākhyātā tāṃ vinā naiva siddhyati /
kavacaṃ mantrasahitaṃ hyapi varṣāyutāyutaiḥ //
2.34.d:
योत्तमा भक्तिराख्याता तां विना नैव सिद्ध्यति ।
कवचं मन्त्रसहितं ह्यपि वर्षायुतायुतैः ॥
2.34.m: Without that which is called highest devotion, / the armor together with the mantra is not accomplished even in myriads upon myriads of years.

2.34.s:
yadyayaṃ bhārgavo bhadre hyagastyānugrahaṃ labhet /
kṛṣṇapremāmṛtaṃ nāma stotramuttamabhaktidam //
2.34.d:
यद्ययं भार्गवो भद्रे ह्यगस्त्यानुग्रहं लभेत् ।
कृष्णप्रेमामृतं नाम स्तोत्रमुत्तमभक्तिदम् ॥
2.34.m: If this Bhārgava, gentle lady, obtains the grace of Agastya, / and understands the hymn named Kṛṣṇapremāmṛta which bestows highest devotion,

2.34.s:
jñātvā ca lapsyate siddhiṃ mantrasya kavacasya ca /
sa munirjñātatattvārthaḥ sānukaṃpo 'bhayapradaḥ //
2.34.d:
ज्ञात्वा च लप्स्यते सिद्धिं मन्त्रस्य कवचस्य च ।
स मुनिर्ज्ञाततत्त्वार्थः सानुकंपो ऽभयप्रदः ॥
2.34.m: he will attain accomplishment of the mantra and the armor; / that sage, knowing the truth of reality, compassionate, bestowing fearlessness,

2.34.s:
upadekṣyati caivainaṃ tattvajñānaṃ mudāvaham /
śrīkṛṣṇacāritaṃ sarvaṃ nāmabhirgrathitaṃ yataḥ //
2.34.d:
उपदेक्ष्यति चैवैनं तत्त्वज्ञानं मुदावहम् ।
श्रीकृष्णचारितं सर्वं नामभिर्ग्रथितं यतः ॥
2.34.m: will teach him the knowledge of reality that brings joy; / since the whole story of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is woven together with names

2.34.s:
kṛṣṇapremāmṛtastotrājjñāsyate 'sya mahāmatiḥ /
tataḥ saṃsiddha kavacau rājanaṃ haihayādhipam //
2.34.d:
कृष्णप्रेमामृतस्तोत्राज्ज्ञास्यते ऽस्य महामतिः ।
ततः संसिद्ध कवचौ राजनं हैहयाधिपम् ॥
2.34.m: in the Kṛṣṇapremāmṛtastotra, this wise one will come to know it; / then, having perfected the armor, having slain the king, the ruler of the Haihayas,

2.34.s:
hatvā saputrāmātyaṃ ca sasuhṛdbalavāhanam /
triḥ saptakṛtvo nirbhūpāṃ kariṣyatyavanīṃ priya //
2.34.d:
हत्वा सपुत्रामात्यं च ससुहृद्बलवाहनम् ।
त्रिः सप्तकृत्वो निर्भूपां करिष्यत्यवनीं प्रिय ॥
2.34.m: along with his sons, ministers, friends, army, and mounts, / he will rid the earth of kings thrice seven times, my dear!"

2.34.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
evamuktvā mṛgo rājanvirarāma mṛgīṃ tataḥ /
ātmano mṛgabhāvasya kāraṇaṃ jñātavāṃśca ha //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya
upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite catustriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 34//
2.34.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
एवमुक्त्वा मृगो राजन्विरराम मृगीं ततः ।
आत्मनो मृगभावस्य कारणं ज्ञातवांश्च ह ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय
उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते चतुस्त्रिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 34॥
2.34.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
Having spoken thus to the doe, O king, the buck then became silent; / and he also knew the cause of his own state as a deer.

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter on the deeds of Bhārgava, in the third Upoddhātapāda of the middle part of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, spoken by Vāyu.

2.35.s:
sagara uvāca
mune paramatattvajñadhyānajñānārthakovida /
bhagavadbhaktisaṃlīnamānasānugrahaḥ kutaḥ //
2.35.d:
सगर उवाच
मुने परमतत्त्वज्ञध्यानज्ञानार्थकोविद ।
भगवद्भक्तिसंलीनमानसानुग्रहः कुतः ॥
2.35.m:
Sagara said:
"O sage, knower of the supreme reality, skilled in the meaning of meditation and knowledge, / whence comes the grace upon those whose minds are absorbed in devotion to the Lord?

2.35.s:
tvayāpi hi mahābhāga yataḥ śaṃsasi satkathāḥ /
śrutvā mṛgamukhātsarvaṃ bhārgavasya viceṣṭitam //
2.35.d:
त्वयापि हि महाभाग यतः शंससि सत्कथाः ।
श्रुत्वा मृगमुखात्सर्वं भार्गवस्य विचेष्टितम् ॥
2.35.m: Indeed, by you too, illustrious one, since you relate good tales; / having heard from the mouth of the deer all the deeds of Bhārgava,

2.35.s:
bhūtaṃ bhavadbhaviṣyaṃ ca nārāyaṇakathānvitam /
punaḥ prapaccha kiṃ nātha tanme vada savistaram //
2.35.d:
भूतं भवद्भविष्यं च नारायणकथान्वितम् ।
पुनः प्रपच्छ किं नाथ तन्मे वद सविस्तरम् ॥
2.35.m: past, present, and future, accompanied by tales of Nārāyaṇa, / what did she ask again, O master? Tell me that in detail."

2.35.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
śṛṇu rājanpravakṣyāmi mṛgasya caritaṃ mahat /
yathā pṛṣṭaṃ tayā so 'syai varṇayāmāsa tattvavit //
2.35.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
शृणु राजन्प्रवक्ष्यामि मृगस्य चरितं महत् ।
यथा पृष्टं तया सो ऽस्यै वर्णयामास तत्त्ववित् ॥
2.35.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
"Listen, O king, I will tell the great story of the deer, / just as it was asked by her, and as he, the knower of truth, described it to her.

2.35.s:
śrutvā tu caritaṃ tasya bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ /
bhūyaḥ prapaccha taṃ kāntaṃ jñānatattvārthamādarāt //
2.35.d:
श्रुत्वा तु चरितं तस्य भार्गवस्य महात्मनः ।
भूयः प्रपच्छ तं कान्तं ज्ञानतत्त्वार्थमादरात् ॥
2.35.m: Having heard the story of that great-souled Bhārgava, / she again questioned her beloved with respect concerning the meaning of the truth of knowledge."

2.35.s:
mṛgyuvāca
sādhusādhu mahābhāga kṛtārthastvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ /
yadasya darśanātte 'dya jātaṃ jñānamatīdriyam //
2.35.d:
मृग्युवाच
साधुसाधु महाभाग कृतार्थस्त्वं न संशयः ।
यदस्य दर्शनात्ते ऽद्य जातं ज्ञानमतीद्रियम् ॥
2.35.m:
The doe said:
"Well done, well done, illustrious one! You have accomplished your goal, there is no doubt, / since from the sight of him this super-sensory knowledge has arisen in you today.

2.35.s:
athātaścātmanaḥ sarvaṃ mamāpi vada kāraṇam /
karmaṇā yena saṃprāptāvāvāṃ tiryagjaniṃ prabho //
2.35.d:
अथातश्चात्मनः सर्वं ममापि वद कारणम् ।
कर्मणा येन संप्राप्तावावां तिर्यग्जनिं प्रभो ॥
2.35.m: Therefore, tell me also the entire reason concerning yourself and me, / through what action we two have obtained birth as animals, O lord."

2.35.s:
iti vākyaṃ samākarṇya priyāyāḥ sa mṛgaḥ svayam /
varṇayāmāsa caritaṃ mṛgyaścaivātmanastadā //
2.35.d:
इति वाक्यं समाकर्ण्य प्रियायाः स मृगः स्वयम् ।
वर्णयामास चरितं मृग्यश्चैवात्मनस्तदा ॥
2.35.m: Having heard this speech of his beloved, that buck himself / then described to the doe her deeds and his own.

2.35.s:
mṛga uvāca
śṛṇu priye mahābhāge yathā'vāṃ mṛgatāṃ gatau /
saṃsāre 'sminnamahābhāge bhāvo 'sya bhavakāraṇam //
2.35.d:
मृग उवाच
शृणु प्रिये महाभागे यथाऽवां मृगतां गतौ ।
संसारे ऽस्मिन्नमहाभागे भावो ऽस्य भवकारणम् ॥
2.35.m:
The buck said:
"Listen, my beloved, illustrious lady, how the two of us attained the state of deer; / in this worldly existence, O fortunate one, one's disposition is the cause of rebirth.

2.35.s:
jīvasya sadasabhdyāṃ hi karmabhyāmāgataḥ smṛtim /
purā draviḍadeśe tu nānāṛddhisamākule //
2.35.d:
जीवस्य सदसभ्द्यां हि कर्मभ्यामागतः स्मृतिम् ।
पुरा द्रविडदेशे तु नानाऋद्धिसमाकुले ॥
2.35.m: It has come to my memory through the good and bad deeds of an embodied soul. / Formerly, in the Draviḍa country, crowded with various prosperities,

2.35.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ kule vāhaṃ jātaḥ kauśikagotriṇām /
pitā me śivadatto 'bhūnnāmnā śāstraviśāradaḥ //
2.35.d:
ब्राह्मणानां कुले वाहं जातः कौशिकगोत्रिणाम् ।
पिता मे शिवदत्तो ऽभून्नाम्ना शास्त्रविशारदः ॥
2.35.m: I was born in a family of brāhmaṇas belonging to the Kauśika gotra. / My father was named Śivadatta, a scholar of the śāstras.

2.35.s:
tasya putrā vayaṃ jātāścatvāro dvijasattamāḥ /
jyeṣṭho rāmo 'nujastasya dhamastasyānu jaḥ pṛthuḥ //
2.35.d:
तस्य पुत्रा वयं जाताश्चत्वारो द्विजसत्तमाः ।
ज्येष्ठो रामो ऽनुजस्तस्य धमस्तस्यानु जः पृथुः ॥
2.35.m: We were born as his four sons, best of dvijas: / the eldest was Rāma, his younger brother was Dhāma, his younger brother was Pṛthu,

2.35.s:
caturtho 'haṃ priye jāto sūrirityabhiviśrutaḥ /
upanīya kramātsarvāñchivadatto mahāyaśāḥ //
2.35.d:
चतुर्थो ऽहं प्रिये जातो सूरिरित्यभिविश्रुतः ।
उपनीय क्रमात्सर्वाञ्छिवदत्तो महायशाः ॥
2.35.m: and I was born the fourth, O beloved, renowned as Sūri. / Having initiated all of them in due order, the highly renowned Śivadatta

2.35.s:
vedānadhyāpayāmāsa sāṃgāṃśca sarahasyakān /
catvāro 'pi vayaṃ tatra vedādhyayanatatparāḥ //
2.35.d:
वेदानध्यापयामास सांगांश्च सरहस्यकान् ।
चत्वारो ऽपि वयं तत्र वेदाध्ययनतत्पराः ॥
2.35.m: taught them the Vedas along with their auxiliary branches and their secret teachings. / All four of us were intent upon Vedic study there,

2.35.s:
guruśuśrūṣaṇe yuktā jātā jñānaparāyaṇāḥ /
gatvāraṇyaṃ phalānyaṃbusamitkuśamṛdo 'nvaham //
2.35.d:
गुरुशुश्रूषणे युक्ता जाता ज्ञानपरायणाः ।
गत्वारण्यं फलान्यंबुसमित्कुशमृदो ऽन्वहम् ॥
2.35.m: devoted to the service of our guru, and absorbed in knowledge. / Having gone to the forest every day for fruits, water, sacrificial fuel, kuśa grass, and clay,

2.35.s:
ānīya pitre dattvātha kurmo 'dhyayanameva hi /
ekadā tu vayaṃ sarve saṃprāptā parvate vane //
2.35.d:
आनीय पित्रे दत्त्वाथ कुर्मो ऽध्ययनमेव हि ।
एकदा तु वयं सर्वे संप्राप्ता पर्वते वने ॥
2.35.m: and having brought them and given them to our father, we would then engage only in study. / Once, however, we all arrived at a forested mountain,

2.35.s:
audbhidaṃ nāma lolakṣi kṛtamālātaṭe sthitam /
sarve snātvā mahānadyāmuṣasi prītamānasāḥ //
2.35.d:
औद्भिदं नाम लोलक्षि कृतमालातटे स्थितम् ।
सर्वे स्नात्वा महानद्यामुषसि प्रीतमानसाः ॥
2.35.m: named Audbhida, O unsteady-eyed one, situated on the bank of the Kṛtamālā. / Having all bathed at dawn in the great river, with delighted minds,

2.35.s:
dattārghāḥ kṛtajapyāśca samārūḍhā nāgottamam /
śālastamālaiḥ priyakaiḥ panasaiḥ kovidārakaiḥ //
2.35.d:
दत्तार्घाः कृतजप्याश्च समारूढा नागोत्तमम् ।
शालस्तमालैः प्रियकैः पनसैः कोविदारकैः ॥
2.35.m: having offered the water libation and performed our recitations, we ascended that best of mountains. / With śāla, tamāla, priyaka, jackfruit, and kovidāra trees,

2.35.s:
saralārjunapūgaiśca kharjūrairnārikelakaiḥ /
jaṃbūbhiḥ sahakāraiśca kaṭphalairbṛhatīdrumaiḥ //
2.35.d:
सरलार्जुनपूगैश्च खर्जूरैर्नारिकेलकैः ।
जंबूभिः सहकारैश्च कट्फलैर्बृहतीद्रुमैः ॥
2.35.m: and with sarala, arjuna, and areca nut palms, dates, coconuts, / rose-apples, mangoes, kaṭphala trees, and bṛhatī plants,

2.35.s:
anyairnānāvidhairvṛkṣaiḥ parārthapratipādakaiḥ /
snigdhacchāyaiḥ samāhṛṣṭanānāpakṣinināditaiḥ //
2.35.d:
अन्यैर्नानाविधैर्वृक्षैः परार्थप्रतिपादकैः ।
स्निग्धच्छायैः समाहृष्टनानापक्षिनिनादितैः ॥
2.35.m: with other trees of various kinds that grant benefits to others, / with soothing shade, resounding with various delighted birds,

2.35.s:
śārdūla haribhirbhallairgaṇḍakairmṛganābhibhiḥ /
gacaindraiḥ śārabhādyaiśca sevitaṃ kandarāgataiḥ //
2.35.d:
शार्दूल हरिभिर्भल्लैर्गण्डकैर्मृगनाभिभिः ।
गचैन्द्रैः शारभाद्यैश्च सेवितं कन्दरागतैः ॥
2.35.m: frequented by tigers, lions, bears, rhinoceroses, and musk-deer, / by lordly elephants and śarabhas and other beasts dwelling in caves,

2.35.s:
mallikāpāṭalākundakarṇikārakadaṃbakaiḥ /
sugandhibhirvṛtaṃ cānyairvātoddhūtaparagibhiḥ //
2.35.d:
मल्लिकापाटलाकुन्दकर्णिकारकदंबकैः ।
सुगन्धिभिर्वृतं चान्यैर्वातोद्धूतपरगिभिः ॥
2.35.m: surrounded by fragrant mallikā, pāṭalā, kunda, karṇikāra, and kadamba flowers, / and others whose pollen was tossed up by the wind,

2.35.s:
nānāmaṇigaṇākīrṇairnīlapītasitāruṇaiḥ /
śṛṅgaiḥ samullikhantaṃ ca vyoma kautukasaṃ yutam //
2.35.d:
नानामणिगणाकीर्णैर्नीलपीतसितारुणैः ।
